3.s:
ūnadvivarṣaṃ nikhanen na kuryād udakaṃ tataḥ /
āśmaśānād anuvrajya itaro jñātibhir vṛtaḥ //
3.d:
ऊनद्विवर्षं निखनेन् न कुर्याद् उदकं ततः ।
आश्मशानाद् अनुव्रज्य इतरो ज्ञातिभिर् वृतः ॥
3.m: One should bury a child under two years old; no water offering should be made thereafter. / Following [the corpse] to the cremation ground, any other person, accompanied by relatives,

3.s:
yamasūktaṃ tathā gāthā japadbhir laukikāgninā /
sa dagdhavya upetaś ced āhitāgnyāvṛtārthavat //
3.d:
यमसूक्तं तथा गाथा जपद्भिर् लौकिकाग्निना ।
स दग्धव्य उपेतश् चेद् आहिताग्न्यावृतार्थवत् ॥
3.m: should be burned with secular fire by those reciting the Yama hymn and sacred verses, / but if initiated, according to the rule of the keeper of sacred fire, with proper rites.

3.s:
saptamād daśamād vāpi jñātayo 'bhyupayanty apaḥ /
apa naḥ śośucad agham anena pitṛdiṅmukhāḥ //
3.d:
सप्तमाद् दशमाद् वापि ज्ञातयो ऽभ्युपयन्त्य् अपः ।
अप नः शोशुचद् अघम् अनेन पितृदिङ्मुखाः ॥
3.m: From the seventh or tenth [degree of kinship], relatives enter the water, / facing the direction of the ancestors, with the verse: 'May our sin burn away.'

3.s:
evaṃ mātāmahācāryapretānām udakakriyā /
kāmodakaṃ sakhiprattāsvasrīyaśvaśurartvijām //
3.d:
एवं मातामहाचार्यप्रेतानाम् उदकक्रिया ।
कामोदकं सखिप्रत्तास्वस्रीयश्वशुरर्त्विजाम् ॥
3.m: Such is the water rite for deceased maternal grandfathers and teachers. / The water offering is optional for friends, married daughters, sisters' sons, fathers-in-law, and sacrificial priests.

3.s:
sakṛt prasiñcanty udakaṃ nāmagotreṇa vāgyatāḥ /
na brahmacāriṇaḥ kuryur udakaṃ patitās tathā //
3.d:
सकृत् प्रसिञ्चन्त्य् उदकं नामगोत्रेण वाग्यताः ।
न ब्रह्मचारिणः कुर्युर् उदकं पतितास् तथा ॥
3.m: Remaining silent, they pour out water once, uttering the name and clan. / Chaste students and outcasts must not perform the water offering.

3.s:
pākhaṇḍyanāśritāḥ stenā bhartṛghnyaḥ kāmagādikāḥ /
surāpya ātmatyāginyo nāśaucodakabhājanāḥ //
3.d:
पाखण्ड्यनाश्रिताः स्तेना भर्तृघ्न्यः कामगादिकाः ।
सुराप्य आत्मत्यागिन्यो नाशौचोदकभाजनाः ॥
3.m: Those who belong to heretical sects, thieves, husband-slayers, unchaste women and the like, / female wine-drinkers, and women who commit suicide are not entitled to impurity or water offerings.

3.s:
kṛtodakān samuttīrṇān mṛduśādvalasaṃsthitān /
snātān apavadeyus tān itihāsaiḥ purātanaiḥ //
3.d:
कृतोदकान् समुत्तीर्णान् मृदुशाद्वलसंस्थितान् ।
स्नातान् अपवदेयुस् तान् इतिहासैः पुरातनैः ॥
3.m: Having offered water, emerged [from it], and sat down on soft green grass, / after bathing, others should console them with ancient legends:

3.s:
mānuṣye kadalīstambhaniḥsāre sāramārgaṇam /
karoti yaḥ sa sammūḍho jalabudbudasaṃnibhe //
3.d:
मानुष्ये कदलीस्तम्भनिःसारे सारमार्गणम् ।
करोति यः स सम्मूढो जलबुद्बुदसंनिभे ॥
3.m: 'Whoever seeks substance in human existence, which is devoid of substance like a plantain stalk / and resembles a water bubble, is completely deluded.

3.s:
pañcadhā saṃbhṛtaḥ kāyo yadi pañcatvam āgataḥ /
karmabhiḥ svaśarīrotthais tatra kā paridevanā //
3.d:
पञ्चधा संभृतः कायो यदि पञ्चत्वम् आगतः ।
कर्मभिः स्वशरीरोत्थैस् तत्र का परिदेवना ॥
3.m: If the body, composed of the five elements, has returned to the five elements / by means of deeds arising from one's own body, what lamentation can there be?

3.s:
gantrī vasumatī nāśam udadhir daivatāni ca /
phenaprakhyaḥ kathaṃ nāśaṃ martyaloko na yāsyati //
3.d:
गन्त्री वसुमती नाशम् उदधिर् दैवतानि च ।
फेनप्रख्यः कथं नाशं मर्त्यलोको न यास्यति ॥
3.m: The earth will go to destruction, as will the ocean and the deities; / how shall the mortal world, resembling foam, not go to destruction?

3.s:
śleṣmāśru bāndhavair muktaṃ preto bhuṅkte yato 'vaśaḥ /
ato na roditavyaṃ hi kriyāḥ kāryāḥ svaśaktitaḥ //
3.d:
श्लेष्माश्रु बान्धवैर् मुक्तं प्रेतो भुङ्क्ते यतो ऽवशः ।
अतो न रोदितव्यं हि क्रियाः कार्याः स्वशक्तितः ॥
3.m: Because the deceased helplessly consumes the phlegm and tears shed by kinsmen, / one must not weep; rather, rites should be performed according to one's capacity.'

3.s:
iti saṃśrutya gaccheyur gṛhaṃ bālapuraḥsarāḥ /
vidaśya nimbapatrāṇi niyatā dvāri veśmanaḥ //
3.d:
इति संश्रुत्य गच्छेयुर् गृहं बालपुरःसराः ।
विदश्य निम्बपत्राणि नियता द्वारि वेश्मनः ॥
3.m: Having listened to this, they should go home, led by the children; / chewing neem leaves, with restrained minds, at the door of the house,

3.s:
ācamyāgnyādi salilaṃ gomayaṃ gaurasarṣapān /
praviśeyuḥ samālabhya kṛtvāśmani padaṃ śanaiḥ //
3.d:
आचम्याग्न्यादि सलिलं गोमयं गौरसर्षपान् ।
प्रविशेयुः समालभ्य कृत्वाश्मनि पदं शनैः ॥
3.m: having sipped water for purification, touching fire, water, cow dung, and white mustard seeds, / and placing a foot gently upon a stone, they should enter.

3.s:
praveśanādikaṃ karma pretasaṃsparśinām api /
icchatāṃ tatkṣaṇāc chuddhiḥ pareṣāṃ snānasaṃyamān //
3.d:
प्रवेशनादिकं कर्म प्रेतसंस्पर्शिनाम् अपि ।
इच्छतां तत्क्षणाच् छुद्धिः परेषां स्नानसंयमान् ॥
3.m: The rite of entering and so forth is also for those who touched the corpse; / for others desiring immediate purification, it is through bathing and self-restraint.

3.s:
ācāryapitṛupādhyāyān nirhṛtyāpi vratī vratī /
saṃkaṭānnaṃ ca nāśnīyān na ca taiḥ saha saṃvaset //
3.d:
आचार्यपितृउपाध्यायान् निर्हृत्यापि व्रती व्रती ।
संकटान्नं च नाश्नीयान् न च तैः सह संवसेत् ॥
3.m: A student under vow who carries out [the corpse of] his preceptors, father, or sub-teachers remains a student under vow; / he must not eat food prepared during impurity, nor live together with them.

3.s:
krītalabdhāśanā bhūmau svapeyus te pṛthak kṣitau /
piṇḍayajñāvṛtā deyaṃ pretāyānnaṃ dinatrayam //
3.d:
क्रीतलब्धाशना भूमौ स्वपेयुस् ते पृथक् क्षितौ ।
पिण्डयज्ञावृता देयं प्रेतायान्नं दिनत्रयम् ॥
3.m: Eating food bought or obtained by begging, they should sleep on the bare earth separately. / According to the procedure of the funeral cake offering, food should be given to the deceased for three days.

3.s:
jalam ekāham ākāśe sthāpyaṃ kṣīraṃ ca mṛnmaye /
vaitānāupāsanāḥ kāryāḥ kriyāś ca śruticodanāt //
3.d:
जलम् एकाहम् आकाशे स्थाप्यं क्षीरं च मृन्मये ।
वैतानाउपासनाः कार्याः क्रियाश् च श्रुतिचोदनात् ॥
3.m: Water and milk in an earthen pot should be placed in the open air for one day. / The Vedic and domestic rites must be performed, as enjoined by revealed scripture.

3.s:
trirātraṃ daśarātraṃ vā śāvam āśaucam iṣyate /
ūnadvivarṣa ubhayoḥ sūtakaṃ mātur eva hi //
3.d:
त्रिरात्रं दशरात्रं वा शावम् आशौचम् इष्यते ।
ऊनद्विवर्ष उभयोः सूतकं मातुर् एव हि ॥
3.m: Death impurity is prescribed for three nights or ten nights. / For a child under two years old, [impurity applies] to both parents; birth impurity, however, is for the mother alone.

3.s:
pitros tu sūtakaṃ mātus tad asṛgdarśanād dhruvam /
tad ahar na praduṣyeta pūrveṣāṃ janmakāraṇāt //
3.d:
पित्रोस् तु सूतकं मातुस् तद् असृग्दर्शनाद् ध्रुवम् ।
तद् अहर् न प्रदुष्येत पूर्वेषां जन्मकारणात् ॥
3.m: Birth impurity belongs to both parents, but surely to the mother because of the appearance of blood; / the day [of birth] does not cause impurity for the father and others on account of the occasion of birth.

3.s:
antarā janmamaraṇe śeṣāhobhir viśudhyati /
garbhasrāve māsatulyā niśāḥ śuddhes tu kāraṇam //
3.d:
अन्तरा जन्ममरणे शेषाहोभिर् विशुध्यति ।
गर्भस्रावे मासतुल्या निशाः शुद्धेस् तु कारणम् ॥
3.m:
If a birth or death occurs in between, one becomes purified after the remaining days.
In the case of a miscarriage, the number of nights equal to the months [of pregnancy] is the cause of purification.

3.s:
hatānāṃ nṛpagoviprair anvakṣaṃ cātmaghātinām /
proṣite kālaśeṣaḥ syāt pūrṇe dattvodakaṃ śuciḥ //
3.d:
हतानां नृपगोविप्रैर् अन्वक्षं चात्मघातिनाम् ।
प्रोषिते कालशेषः स्यात् पूर्णे दत्त्वोदकं शुचिः ॥
3.m:
For those killed by kings, cows, or Brahmins, and for suicides, [purification is] immediate.
When [a kinsman dies] abroad, [the period of impurity] should be the remainder of the time; once [that period has] fully passed, one is pure after offering water.

3.s:
kṣatrasya dvādaśāhāni viśaḥ pañcadaśaiva tu /
triṃśaddināni śūdrasya tadardhaṃ nyāyavartinaḥ //
3.d:
क्षत्रस्य द्वादशाहानि विशः पञ्चदशैव तु ।
त्रिंशद्दिनानि शूद्रस्य तदर्धं न्यायवर्तिनः ॥
3.m:
Twelve days are prescribed for a Kshatriya, and fifteen for a Vaishya,
thirty days for a Shudra, and half of that for one who follows righteous conduct.

3.s:
ādantajanmanaḥ sadyā acūḍān naiśikī smṛtā /
trirātram āvratādeśād daśarātram ataḥ param //
3.d:
आदन्तजन्मनः सद्या अचूडान् नैशिकी स्मृता ।
त्रिरात्रम् आव्रतादेशाद् दशरात्रम् अतः परम् ॥
3.m:
Until the eruption of teeth [purification is] immediate; until tonsure it is taught to be one night;
three nights until the investiture of vows; beyond that, ten nights.

3.s:
ahas tv adattakanyāsu bāleṣu ca viśodhanam /
gurvantevāsyanūcānam ātulaśrotriyeṣu ca //
3.d:
अहस् त्व् अदत्तकन्यासु बालेषु च विशोधनम् ।
गुर्वन्तेवास्यनूचानम् आतुलश्रोत्रियेषु च ॥
3.m:
One day is the purifier for unmarried girls and young boys,
and for a guru, a resident pupil, a learned teacher, a maternal uncle, and a Vedic scholar;

3.s:
anauraseṣu putreṣu bhāryāsv anyagatāsu ca /
nivāsarājani prete tad ahaḥ śuddhikāraṇam //
3.d:
अनौरसेषु पुत्रेषु भार्यास्व् अन्यगतासु च ।
निवासराजनि प्रेते तद् अहः शुद्धिकारणम् ॥
3.m:
and for sons not born of one's own body, wives gone to another,
and when the king of one's place of residence has died, that day is the cause of purification.

3.s:
brāhmaṇenānugantavyo na śūdro na dvijaḥ kvacit /
anugamyāmbhasi snātvā spṛṣṭvāgniṃ ghṛtabhuk śuciḥ //
3.d:
ब्राह्मणेनानुगन्तव्यो न शूद्रो न द्विजः क्वचित् ।
अनुगम्याम्भसि स्नात्वा स्पृष्ट्वाग्निं घृतभुक् शुचिः ॥
3.m:
A Brahmin should never follow the corpse of a Shudra, nor that of a twice-born.
If he follows [one], he becomes pure after bathing in water, touching fire, and eating ghee.

3.s:
mahīpatīnāṃ nāśaucaṃ hatānāṃ vidyutā tathā /
gobrāhmaṇārthaṃ saṃgrāme yasya cecchati bhūmipaḥ //
3.d:
महीपतीनां नाशौचं हतानां विद्युता तथा ।
गोब्राह्मणार्थं संग्रामे यस्य चेच्छति भूमिपः ॥
3.m:
There is no impurity for rulers of the earth, nor for those killed by lightning,
nor in battle for the sake of cows and Brahmins, nor for anyone the ruler of the earth desires.

3.s:
ṛtvijāṃ dīkṣitānāṃ ca yajñiyaṃ karma kurvatām /
satrivratibrahmacāridātṛbrahmavidāṃ tathā //
3.d:
ऋत्विजां दीक्षितानां च यज्ञियं कर्म कुर्वताम् ।
सत्रिव्रतिब्रह्मचारिदातृब्रह्मविदां तथा ॥
3.m:
Nor for sacrificial priests and initiated persons performing sacrificial rites;
likewise for those engaged in a sacrificial session, vow-holders, chaste students, donors, and knowers of Brahman;

3.s:
dāne vivāhe yajñe ca saṃgrāme deśaviplave /
āpadyapi hi kaṣṭāyāṃ sadyaḥ śaucaṃ vidhīyate //
3.d:
दाने विवाहे यज्ञे च संग्रामे देशविप्लवे ।
आपद्यपि हि कष्टायां सद्यः शौचं विधीयते ॥
3.m:
at a gift, a marriage, and a sacrifice; in battle, during civil disturbance,
and in dire distress, immediate purification is prescribed.

3.s:
udakyāśucibhiḥ snāyāt saṃspṛṣṭas tair upaspṛśet /
abliṅgāni japec caiva gāyatrīṃ manasā sakṛt //
3.d:
उदक्याशुचिभिः स्नायात् संस्पृष्टस् तैर् उपस्पृशेत् ।
अब्लिङ्गानि जपेच् चैव गायत्रीं मनसा सकृत् ॥
3.m:
If touched by a menstruating woman or impure persons, one should bathe and sip water for purification;
and one should mutter the water hymns and the Gāyatrī once in thought.

3.s:
kālo 'gniḥ karma mṛd vāyur mano jñānaṃ tapo jalam /
paścāt tāpo nirāhāraḥ sarve 'mī śuddhihetavaḥ //
3.d:
कालो ऽग्निः कर्म मृद् वायुर् मनो ज्ञानं तपो जलम् ।
पश्चात् तापो निराहारः सर्वे ऽमी शुद्धिहेतवः ॥
3.m:
Time, fire, rite, earth, wind, mind, knowledge, austerity, water,
repentance, and abstention from food: all these are causes of purification.

3.s:
akāryakāriṇāṃ dānaṃ vego nadyāś ca śuddhikṛt /
śodhyasya mṛc ca toyaṃ ca saṃnyāso vai dvijanmanām //
3.d:
अकार्यकारिणां दानं वेगो नद्याश् च शुद्धिकृत् ।
शोध्यस्य मृच् च तोयं च संन्यासो वै द्विजन्मनाम् ॥
3.m:
For those who have committed misdeeds, giving is the purifier; and for a river, its current;
for an object to be cleansed, earth and water; and renunciation, indeed, for the twice-born.

3.s:
tapo vedavidāṃ kṣāntir viduṣāṃ varṣmaṇo jalam /
japaḥ pracchannapānānāṃ manasaḥ satyam ucyate //
3.d:
तपो वेदविदां क्षान्तिर् विदुषां वर्ष्मणो जलम् ।
जपः प्रच्छन्नपानानां मनसः सत्यम् उच्यते ॥
3.m:
Austerity is said to be the purifier of knowers of the Veda; forbearance, of the wise; water, of the body;
muttering, of secret drinkers; truth, of the mind.

3.s:
bhūtātmanas tapovidye buddher jñānaṃ viśodhanam /
kṣetrajñasyeśvarajñānād viśuddhiḥ paramā matā //
3.d:
भूतात्मनस् तपोविद्ये बुद्धेर् ज्ञानं विशोधनम् ।
क्षेत्रज्ञस्येश्वरज्ञानाद् विशुद्धिः परमा मता ॥
3.m:
Austerity and sacred knowledge are the purifier of the individual self; knowledge, of the intellect;
from the knowledge of the Lord, supreme purification of the knower of the field is recognized.

3.s:
kṣātreṇa karmaṇā jīved viśāṃ vāpy āpadi dvijaḥ /
nistīrya tām athātmānaṃ pāvayitvā nyaset pathi //
3.d:
क्षात्रेण कर्मणा जीवेद् विशां वाप्य् आपदि द्विजः ।
निस्तीर्य ताम् अथात्मानं पावयित्वा न्यसेत् पथि ॥
3.m:
In distress, a twice-born may live by the work of a Kshatriya or even of a Vaishya;
having crossed over it, he should purify himself and set himself upon the proper path.

3.s:
phalopalakṣaumasomamanuṣyāpūpavīrudhaḥ /
tilaudanarasakṣārān dadhi kṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ jalam //
3.d:
फलोपलक्षौमसोममनुष्यापूपवीरुधः ।
तिलौदनरसक्षारान् दधि क्षीरं घृतं जलम् ॥
3.m:
Fruits, gems, linen, soma, human beings, cakes, creepers,
sesame, boiled rice, essences, alkaline salts, curds, milk, ghee, water,

3.s:
śastrāsavamadhūcchiṣṭaṃ madhu lākṣā ca barhiṣaḥ /
mṛccarmapuṣpakutapakeśatakraviṣakṣitiḥ //
3.d:
शस्त्रासवमधूच्छिष्टं मधु लाक्षा च बर्हिषः ।
मृच्चर्मपुष्पकुतपकेशतक्रविषक्षितिः ॥
3.m:
weapons, spirituous liquor, beeswax, honey, lac, kuśa grass,
earth, skins, flowers, woollen blankets, hair, buttermilk, poison, land,

3.s:
kauśeyanīlalavaṇamāṃsaikaśaphasīsakān /
śakārdrauṣadhipiṇyākapaśugandhāṃs tathaiva ca //
3.d:
कौशेयनीललवणमांसैकशफसीसकान् ।
शकार्द्रौषधिपिण्याकपशुगन्धांस् तथैव च ॥
3.m:
silk, indigo, salt, meat, single-hoofed animals, lead,
dung, moist medicinal herbs, oil-cake, beasts, and perfumes—

3.s:
vaiśyavṛttyāpi jīvan no vikrīṇīta kadācana /
dharmārthaṃ vikrayaṃ neyās tilā dhānyena tatsamāḥ //
3.d:
वैश्यवृत्त्यापि जीवन् नो विक्रीणीत कदाचन ।
धर्मार्थं विक्रयं नेयास् तिला धान्येन तत्समाः ॥
3.m:
even when living by the occupation of a Vaishya, he must never sell these.
For religious purposes, sesame may be bartered for equal grain.

3.s:
lākṣālavaṇamāṃsāni patanīyāni vikraye /
pāyo dadhi ca madyaṃ ca hīnavarṇakarāṇi tu //
3.d:
लाक्षालवणमांसानि पतनीयानि विक्रये ।
पायो दधि च मद्यं च हीनवर्णकराणि तु ॥
3.m:
Lac, salt, and meat cause degradation when sold;
milk, curds, and intoxicating drink make one lower in class.

3.s:
āpadgataḥ saṃpragṛhṇan bhuñjāno vā yatas tataḥ /
na lipyetainasā vipro jvalanārkasamo hi saḥ //
3.d:
आपद्गतः संप्रगृह्णन् भुञ्जानो वा यतस् ततः ।
न लिप्येतैनसा विप्रो ज्वलनार्कसमो हि सः ॥
3.m:
A Brahmin in distress, accepting gifts or eating from anyone whatsoever,
is not tainted by sin, for he is equal to fire and the sun.

3.s:
kṛṣiḥ śilpaṃ bhṛtir vidyā kusīdaṃ śakaṭaṃ giriḥ /
sevānūpaṃ nṛpo bhaikṣam āpattau jīvanāni tu //
3.d:
कृषिः शिल्पं भृतिर् विद्या कुसीदं शकटं गिरिः ।
सेवानूपं नृपो भैक्षम् आपत्तौ जीवनानि तु ॥
3.m:
Agriculture, crafts, hired labour, teaching, money-lending, carting, [gathering in] mountains,
service, [clearing] wetlands, the king, and begging are livelihoods in distress.

3.s:
bubhukṣitas tryahaṃ sthitvā dhānyam abrāhmaṇād haret /
pratigṛhya tad ākhyeyam abhiyuktena dharmataḥ //
3.d:
बुभुक्षितस् त्र्यहं स्थित्वा धान्यम् अब्राह्मणाद् हरेत् ।
प्रतिगृह्य तद् आख्येयम् अभियुक्तेन धर्मतः ॥
3.m:
Remaining hungry for three days, he may take grain from a non-Brahmin;
having taken it, if charged, he must declare it according to duty.

3.s:
tasya vṛttaṃ kulaṃ śīlaṃ śrutam adhyayanaṃ tapaḥ /
jñātvā rājā kuṭumbaṃ ca dharmyāṃ vṛttiṃ prakalpayet //
3.d:
तस्य वृत्तं कुलं शीलं श्रुतम् अध्ययनं तपः ।
ज्ञात्वा राजा कुटुम्बं च धर्म्यां वृत्तिं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
3.m:
Having ascertained his conduct, family, character, learning, recitation, austerity,
and household, the king should assign him a righteous livelihood.

3.s:
sutavinyastapatnīkas tayā vānugato vanam /
vānaprastho brahmacārī sāgniḥ sopāsano vrajet //
3.d:
सुतविन्यस्तपत्नीकस् तया वानुगतो वनम् ।
वानप्रस्थो ब्रह्मचारी साग्निः सोपासनो व्रजेत् ॥
3.m:
Entrusting his wife to his son or accompanied by her,
the forest-dweller, remaining chaste, should go to the forest with his sacred fire and his domestic ritual.

3.s:
aphālakṛṣtenāgnīṃś ca pitṝn devātithīn api /
bhṛtyāṃś ca tarpayet śmaśrujaṭālomabhṛd ātmavān //
3.d:
अफालकृष्तेनाग्नींश् च पितॄन् देवातिथीन् अपि ।
भृत्यांश् च तर्पयेत् श्मश्रुजटालोमभृद् आत्मवान् ॥
3.m:
With food not grown by plowing, self-controlled, bearing a beard, matted hair, and body hair,
he should gratify the fires, the ancestors, the gods, guests, and dependants.

3.s:
ahno māsasya ṣaṇṇāṃ vā tathā saṃvatsarasya vā /
arthasya saṃcayaṃ kuryāt kṛtam āśvayuje tyajet //
3.d:
अह्नो मासस्य षण्णां वा तथा संवत्सरस्य वा ।
अर्थस्य संचयं कुर्यात् कृतम् आश्वयुजे त्यजेत् ॥
3.m:
He may make a hoard of goods for a day, for a month, for six months,
or for a year; what has been gathered he should discard in the month of Āśvayuja.

3.s:
dāntas triṣavaṇasnāyī nivṛttaś ca pratigrahāt /
svādhyāyavān dānaśīlaḥ sarvasattvahite rataḥ //
3.d:
दान्तस् त्रिषवणस्नायी निवृत्तश् च प्रतिग्रहात् ।
स्वाध्यायवान् दानशीलः सर्वसत्त्वहिते रतः ॥
3.m:
Self-restrained, bathing at the three junctures of the day, retired from accepting gifts,
devoted to Vedic study, disposed to give, intent on the welfare of all beings,

3.s:
dantolūkhalikaḥ kālapakvāśī vāśmakuṭṭakaḥ /
śrautraṃ smārtaṃ phalasnehaiḥ karma kuryāt tathā kriyāḥ //
3.d:
दन्तोलूखलिकः कालपक्वाशी वाश्मकुट्टकः ।
श्रौत्रं स्मार्तं फलस्नेहैः कर्म कुर्यात् तथा क्रियाः ॥
3.m:
using his teeth as a mortar or eating what ripens in time or crushing with a stone,
he should perform Vedic and traditional rites and ceremonies with oils from fruits.

3.s:
cāndrāyaṇair nayet kālaṃ kṛcchrair vā vartayet sadā /
pakṣe gate vāpy aśnīyān māse vāhani vā gate //
3.d:
चान्द्रायणैर् नयेत् कालं कृच्छ्रैर् वा वर्तयेत् सदा ।
पक्षे गते वाप्य् अश्नीयान् मासे वाहनि वा गते ॥
3.m:
He should pass time with lunar penances or always live by penitential hardships;
or he may eat after a fortnight has passed, or after a month, or after a day.

3.s:
svapyād bhūmau śucī rātrau divā saṃprapadair nayet /
sthānāsanavihārair vā yogābhyāsena vā tathā //
3.d:
स्वप्याद् भूमौ शुची रात्रौ दिवा संप्रपदैर् नयेत् ।
स्थानासनविहारैर् वा योगाभ्यासेन वा तथा ॥
3.m:
He should sleep on the bare ground, pure, by night, and by day spend time on the tips of his toes,
or by standing, sitting, walking, or by the practice of yoga.

3.s:
grīṣme pañcāgnimadhyastho varṣāsu sthaṇḍileśayaḥ /
ārdravāsās tu hemante śaktyā vāpi tapaś caret //
3.d:
ग्रीष्मे पञ्चाग्निमध्यस्थो वर्षासु स्थण्डिलेशयः ।
आर्द्रवासास् तु हेमन्ते शक्त्या वापि तपश् चरेत् ॥
3.m:
In summer standing in the midst of five fires, in the rainy season lying on the bare ground,
and in winter wearing wet clothes, or he may perform austerity according to his ability.

3.s:
yaḥ kaṇṭakair vitudati candanair yaś ca liṃpati /
akruddho 'parituṣṭaś ca samastasya ca tasya ca //
3.d:
यः कण्टकैर् वितुदति चन्दनैर् यश् च लिंपति ।
अक्रुद्धो ऽपरितुष्टश् च समस्तस्य च तस्य च ॥
3.m:
Neither angry at the one who pierces him with thorns,
nor pleased with the one who smears him with sandalwood, he is equal to both this one and that.

3.s:
agnīn vāpy ātmasātkṛtvā vṛkṣāvāso mitāśanaḥ /
vānaprasthagṛheṣv eva yātrārthaṃ bhaikṣam ācaret //
3.d:
अग्नीन् वाप्य् आत्मसात्कृत्वा वृक्षावासो मिताशनः ।
वानप्रस्थगृहेष्व् एव यात्रार्थं भैक्षम् आचरेत् ॥
3.m:
Or, having interiorized the fires, dwelling at the foot of trees, eating moderately,
he should beg alms for subsistence solely from the houses of forest-dwellers;

3.s:
grāmād āhṛtya vā grāsān aṣṭau bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ /
vāyubhakṣaḥ prāgudīcīṃ gacched vāvarṣmasaṃkṣayāt //
3.d:
ग्रामाद् आहृत्य वा ग्रासान् अष्टौ भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ।
वायुभक्षः प्रागुदीचीं गच्छेद् वावर्ष्मसंक्षयात् ॥
3.m:
or, having brought eight mouthfuls from a village, he should eat them restrained in speech;
or, feeding on air, he should walk toward the northeast until the destruction of his body.

3.s:
vanād gṛhād vā kṛtveṣṭiṃ sārvavedasadakṣiṇām /
prājāpatyāṃ tadante tān agnīn āropya cātmani //
3.d:
वनाद् गृहाद् वा कृत्वेष्टिं सार्ववेदसदक्षिणाम् ।
प्राजापत्यां तदन्ते तान् अग्नीन् आरोप्य चात्मनि ॥
3.m:
From the forest or from the house, having performed the Prājāpatya sacrifice
with all one's possessions as the sacrificial gift, and at its conclusion having deposited those fires within oneself,

3.s:
adhītavedo japakṛt putravān annado 'gnimān /
śaktyā ca yajñakṛn mokṣe manaḥ kuryāt tu nānyathā //
3.d:
अधीतवेदो जपकृत् पुत्रवान् अन्नदो ऽग्निमान् ।
शक्त्या च यज्ञकृन् मोक्षे मनः कुर्यात् तु नान्यथा ॥
3.m:
having studied the Veda, muttered prayers, fathered sons, given food, maintained fires,
and offered sacrifices according to his ability, he should set his mind on liberation—not otherwise.

3.s:
sarvabhūtahitaḥ śāntas tridaṇḍī sakamaṇḍaluḥ /
ekārāmaḥ parivrajya bhikṣārthī grāmam āśrayet //
3.d:
सर्वभूतहितः शान्तस् त्रिदण्डी सकमण्डलुः ।
एकारामः परिव्रज्य भिक्षार्थी ग्रामम् आश्रयेत् ॥
3.m:
Beneficent to all beings, tranquil, carrying three staves and a water pot,
delighting in solitude, having renounced, seeking alms, he should resort to a village.

3.s:
apramattaś cared bhaikṣaṃ sāyāhne 'nabhilakṣitaḥ /
rahite bhikṣukair grāme yātrāmātram alolupaḥ //
3.d:
अप्रमत्तश् चरेद् भैक्षं सायाह्ने ऽनभिलक्षितः ।
रहिते भिक्षुकैर् ग्रामे यात्रामात्रम् अलोलुपः ॥
3.m:
Vigilant, unobserved, in the evening, in a village free of beggars,
not greedy, he should beg alms only for sustenance.

3.s:
yatipātrāṇi mṛdveṇudārvalābumayāni ca /
salilaṃ śuddhir eteṣāṃ govālaiś cāvagharṣaṇam //
3.d:
यतिपात्राणि मृद्वेणुदार्वलाबुमयानि च ।
सलिलं शुद्धिर् एतेषां गोवालैश् चावघर्षणम् ॥
3.m:
The vessels of an ascetic are made of earth, bamboo, wood, or gourd;
purification of these is by water and scrubbing with cow-hair.

3.s:
saṃnirudhyendriyagrāmaṃ rāgadveṣau prahāya ca /
bhayaṃ hitvā ca bhūtānām amṛtībhavati dvijaḥ //
3.d:
संनिरुध्येन्द्रियग्रामं रागद्वेषौ प्रहाय च ।
भयं हित्वा च भूतानाम् अमृतीभवति द्विजः ॥
3.m:
Restraining the collection of sense organs, abandoning passion and aversion,
and removing fear from living beings, a twice-born becomes immortal.

3.s:
kartavyāśayaśuddhis tu bhikṣukeṇa viśeṣataḥ /
jñānotpattinimittatvāt svātantryakaraṇāya ca //
3.d:
कर्तव्याशयशुद्धिस् तु भिक्षुकेण विशेषतः ।
ज्ञानोत्पत्तिनिमित्तत्वात् स्वातन्त्र्यकरणाय च ॥
3.m:
Purification of disposition, especially, must be cultivated by a mendicant,
because it is the cause for the arising of knowledge and for the attainment of spiritual autonomy.

3.s:
avekṣyā garbhavāsāś ca karmajā gatayas tathā /
ādhayo vyādhayaḥ kleśā jarā rūpaviparyayaḥ //
3.d:
अवेक्ष्या गर्भवासाश् च कर्मजा गतयस् तथा ।
आधयो व्याधयः क्लेशा जरा रूपविपर्ययः ॥
3.m:
Dwellings in the womb should be observed, and the states resulting from karma,
worries, diseases, afflictions, old age, the decay of physical form,

3.s:
bhavo jātisahasreṣu priyāpriyaviparyayaḥ /
dhyānayogena saṃpaśyet sūkṣma ātmātmani sthitaḥ //
3.d:
भवो जातिसहस्रेषु प्रियाप्रियविपर्ययः ।
ध्यानयोगेन संपश्येत् सूक्ष्म आत्मात्मनि स्थितः ॥
3.m:
rebirth in thousands of wombs, and the reversal of the agreeable and disagreeable;
through the discipline of meditation he should perceive the subtle Self abiding in the self.

3.s:
nāśramaḥ kāraṇaṃ dharme kriyamāṇo bhaved hi saḥ /
ato yad ātmano 'pathyaṃ pareṣāṃ na tad ācaret //
3.d:
नाश्रमः कारणं धर्मे क्रियमाणो भवेद् हि सः ।
अतो यद् आत्मनो ऽपथ्यं परेषां न तद् आचरेत् ॥
3.m:
The stage of life is not the cause in duty; duty is what is actually done.
Therefore, what is disagreeable to oneself one should not do to others.

3.s:
satyam asteyam akrodho hrīḥ śaucaṃ dhīr dhṛtir damaḥ /
saṃyatendriyatā vidyā dharmaḥ sarva udāhṛtaḥ //
3.d:
सत्यम् अस्तेयम् अक्रोधो ह्रीः शौचं धीर् धृतिर् दमः ।
संयतेन्द्रियता विद्या धर्मः सर्व उदाहृतः ॥
3.m:
Truthfulness, non-stealing, freedom from anger, modesty, purification, wisdom, steadfastness, self-restraint,
control of the senses, knowledge: this is declared to be the whole of duty.

3.s:
niḥsaranti yathā lohapiṇḍāt taptāt sphuliṅgakāḥ /
sakāśād ātmanas tadvad ātmānaḥ prabhavanti hi //
3.d:
निःसरन्ति यथा लोहपिण्डात् तप्तात् स्फुलिङ्गकाः ।
सकाशाद् आत्मनस् तद्वद् आत्मानः प्रभवन्ति हि ॥
3.m: Just as sparks burst forth from a glowing lump of iron, / so indeed do individual selves issue forth from the Self.

3.s:
tatrātmā hi svayaṃ kiṃcit karma kiṃcit svabhāvataḥ /
karoti kiṃcid abhyāsād dharmādharmobhayātmakam //
3.d:
तत्रात्मा हि स्वयं किंचित् कर्म किंचित् स्वभावतः ।
करोति किंचिद् अभ्यासाद् धर्माधर्मोभयात्मकम् ॥
3.m: There the self performs actions: some on its own, some from inherent nature, / and some from habitual practice, consisting of both duty and non-duty.

3.s:
nimittam akṣaraḥ kartā boddhā guṇī vaśī /
ajaḥ śarīragrahaṇāt sa jāta iti kīrtyate //
3.d:
निमित्तम् अक्षरः कर्ता बोद्धा गुणी वशी ।
अजः शरीरग्रहणात् स जात इति कीर्त्यते ॥
3.m: The instrumental cause, imperishable, the agent, the knower, possessing qualities, self-controlled, / unborn—it is spoken of as 'born' only from its taking up of a body.

3.s:
sargādau sa yathākāśaṃ vāyuṃ jyotir jalaṃ mahīm /
sṛjaty ekottaraguṇāṃs tathādatte bhavann api //
3.d:
सर्गादौ स यथाकाशं वायुं ज्योतिर् जलं महीम् ।
सृजत्य् एकोत्तरगुणांस् तथादत्ते भवन्न् अपि ॥
3.m: Just as in the beginning of creation it produces ether, air, fire, water, and earth, / each having one quality more than the last, so taking birth it assumes them.

3.s:
āhutyāpyāyate sūryaḥ sūryād vṛṣṭir athauṣadhiḥ /
tad annaṃ rasarūpeṇa śukratvam adhigacchati //
3.d:
आहुत्याप्यायते सूर्यः सूर्याद् वृष्टिर् अथौषधिः ।
तद् अन्नं रसरूपेण शुक्रत्वम् अधिगच्छति ॥
3.m: By the offering the sun is nourished; from the sun comes rain, and then plants; / that food, through transformation into chyle, attains the state of semen.

3.s:
strīpuṃsayos tu saṃyoge viśuddhe śukraśoṇite /
pañcadhātūn svayaṃ ṣaṣṭha ādatte yugapat prabhuḥ //
3.d:
स्त्रीपुंसयोस् तु संयोगे विशुद्धे शुक्रशोणिते ।
पञ्चधातून् स्वयं षष्ठ आदत्ते युगपत् प्रभुः ॥
3.m: In the union of man and woman, when semen and menstrual blood are pure, / the Lord himself, as the sixth, assumes the five elements all at once.

3.s:
indriyāṇi manaḥ prāṇo jñānam āyuḥ sukhaṃ dhṛtiḥ /
dhāraṇā preraṇaṃ duḥkham icchāhaṃkāra eva ca //
3.d:
इन्द्रियाणि मनः प्राणो ज्ञानम् आयुः सुखं धृतिः ।
धारणा प्रेरणं दुःखम् इच्छाहंकार एव च ॥
3.m: The senses, mind, vital breath, knowledge, lifespan, pleasure, steadfastness, / retention, impulse, pain, desire, and egoism,

3.s:
prayatna ākṛtir varṇaḥ svaradveṣau bhavābhavau /
tasyaitad ātmajaṃ sarvam anāder ādim icchataḥ //
3.d:
प्रयत्न आकृतिर् वर्णः स्वरद्वेषौ भवाभवौ ।
तस्यैतद् आत्मजं सर्वम् अनादेर् आदिम् इच्छतः ॥
3.m: effort, bodily form, complexion, voice, aversion, prosperity and ruin— / all this is born of the Self for him who, though beginningless, wishes for a beginning.

3.s:
prathame māsi saṃkledabhūto dhātuvimūrcchitaḥ /
māsy arbudaṃ dvitīye tu tṛtīye 'ṅgendriyair yutaḥ //
3.d:
प्रथमे मासि संक्लेदभूतो धातुविमूर्च्छितः ।
मास्य् अर्बुदं द्वितीये तु तृतीये ऽङ्गेन्द्रियैर् युतः ॥
3.m: In the first month it is liquefied, compounded of the elements; / in the second month it is a lump; and in the third it is endowed with limbs and senses.

3.s:
ākāśāl lāghavaṃ saukṣmyaṃ śabdaṃ śrotraṃ balādikam /
vāyoś ca sparśanaṃ ceṣṭāṃ vyūhanaṃ raukṣyam eva ca //
3.d:
आकाशाल् लाघवं सौक्ष्म्यं शब्दं श्रोत्रं बलादिकम् ।
वायोश् च स्पर्शनं चेष्टां व्यूहनं रौक्ष्यम् एव च ॥
3.m: From ether it takes lightness, subtlety, sound, the ear, and bodily force; / and from air touch, movement, physical organisation, and dryness;

3.s:
pittāt tu darśanaṃ paktim auṣṇyaṃ rūpaṃ prakāśitām /
rasāt tu rasanaṃ śaityaṃ snehaṃ kledaṃ samārdavam //
3.d:
पित्तात् तु दर्शनं पक्तिम् औष्ण्यं रूपं प्रकाशिताम् ।
रसात् तु रसनं शैत्यं स्नेहं क्लेदं समार्दवम् ॥
3.m: from bile sight, digestion, heat, colour, and brightness; / from moisture taste, coldness, unctuousness, liquidity, and softness;

3.s:
bhūmer gandhaṃ tathā ghrāṇaṃ gauravaṃ mūrtim eva ca /
ātmā gṛhṇāty ajaḥ sarvaṃ tṛtīye spandate tataḥ //
3.d:
भूमेर् गन्धं तथा घ्राणं गौरवं मूर्तिम् एव च ।
आत्मा गृह्णात्य् अजः सर्वं तृतीये स्पन्दते ततः ॥
3.m: from earth smell, the organ of scent, heaviness, and solid form— / the unborn Self assumes all this; then in the third month it stirs.

3.s:
dauhṛdasyāpradānena garbho doṣam avāpnuyāt /
vairūpyaṃ maraṇaṃ vāpi tasmāt kāryaṃ priyaṃ striyāḥ //
3.d:
दौहृदस्याप्रदानेन गर्भो दोषम् अवाप्नुयात् ।
वैरूप्यं मरणं वापि तस्मात् कार्यं प्रियं स्त्रियाः ॥
3.m: Through not granting the pregnancy longings, the foetus may incur a defect, / deformity, or even death; therefore, one must do what is pleasing to the woman.

3.s:
sthairyaṃ caturthe tv aṅgānāṃ pañcame śoṇitodbhavaḥ /
ṣaṣṭhe balasya varṇasya nakharomṇāṃ ca saṃbhavaḥ //
3.d:
स्थैर्यं चतुर्थे त्व् अङ्गानां पञ्चमे शोणितोद्भवः ।
षष्ठे बलस्य वर्णस्य नखरोम्णां च संभवः ॥
3.m: In the fourth month comes firmness of the limbs; in the fifth, the production of blood; / in the sixth, the emergence of strength, complexion, nails, and hair.

3.s:
manaścaitanyayukto 'sau nāḍīsnāyuśirāyutaḥ /
saptame cāṣṭame caiva tvaṅmāṃsasmṛtimān api //
3.d:
मनश्चैतन्ययुक्तो ऽसौ नाडीस्नायुशिरायुतः ।
सप्तमे चाष्टमे चैव त्वङ्मांसस्मृतिमान् अपि ॥
3.m: Endowed with mind and consciousness, furnished with vessels, ligaments, and veins / in the seventh and eighth months, it is also endowed with skin, flesh, and memory.

3.s:
punar dhātrīṃ punar gharmam ojas tasya pradhāvati /
aṣṭame māsy ato garbho jātaḥ prāṇair viyujyate //
3.d:
पुनर् धात्रीं पुनर् घर्मम् ओजस् तस्य प्रधावति ।
अष्टमे मास्य् अतो गर्भो जातः प्राणैर् वियुज्यते ॥
3.m: Its vitality runs repeatedly to the mother and repeatedly to the foetus; / hence, if born in the eighth month, the child is deprived of life.

3.s:
navame daśame vāpi prabalaiḥ sūtimārutaiḥ /
niḥsāryate bāṇa iva yantracchidreṇa sajvaraḥ //
3.d:
नवमे दशमे वापि प्रबलैः सूतिमारुतैः ।
निःसार्यते बाण इव यन्त्रच्छिद्रेण सज्वरः ॥
3.m: In the ninth or tenth month, by the powerful winds of delivery, / it is expelled like an arrow through the opening of the birth canal, suffering fever.

3.s:
tasya ṣoḍhā śarīrāṇi śaṭ tvaco dhārayanti ca /
saḍaṅgāni tathāsthnāṃ ca saha ṣaṣṭyā śatatrayam //
3.d:
तस्य षोढा शरीराणि शट् त्वचो धारयन्ति च ।
सडङ्गानि तथास्थ्नां च सह षष्ट्या शतत्रयम् ॥
3.m: Its bodies are sixfold, six layers of skin support them, / six are the major limbs, and there are three hundred and sixty bones.

3.s:
sthālaiḥ saha catuḥṣaṣṭir dantā vai viṃśatir nakhāḥ /
pāṇipādaśalākāś ca teṣāṃ sthānacatuṣṭayam //
3.d:
स्थालैः सह चतुःषष्टिर् दन्ता वै विंशतिर् नखाः ।
पाणिपादशलाकाश् च तेषां स्थानचतुष्टयम् ॥
3.m: There are sixty-four teeth together with their sockets, twenty nails, / and the small bones of the hands and feet, which have four locations.

3.s:
ṣaṣṭyaṅgulīnāṃ dve pārṣṇyor gulpheṣu ca catuṣṭayam /
catvāryaratnikāsthīni jaṅghayos tāvad eva tu //
3.d:
षष्ट्यङ्गुलीनां द्वे पार्ष्ण्योर् गुल्फेषु च चतुष्टयम् ।
चत्वार्यरत्निकास्थीनि जङ्घयोस् तावद् एव तु ॥
3.m: There are sixty bones of the digits, two in the heels, four in the ankles, / four bones in the forearms, and just as many in the shanks.

3.s:
dve dve jānukapoloruphalakāṃsasamudbhave /
akṣatālūṣake śroṇīphalake ca vinirdiśet //
3.d:
द्वे द्वे जानुकपोलोरुफलकांससमुद्भवे ।
अक्षतालूषके श्रोणीफलके च विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
3.m: One should point out two each in the knees, cheeks, thighs, shoulder blades, collarbones, / eye sockets, palate, and hip bones.

3.s:
bhagāsthy ekaṃ tathā pṛṣṭhe catvāriṃśac ca pañca ca /
grīvā pañcadaśāsthiḥ syāj jatrv ekaikaṃ tathā hanuḥ //
3.d:
भगास्थ्य् एकं तथा पृष्ठे चत्वारिंशच् च पञ्च च ।
ग्रीवा पञ्चदशास्थिः स्याज् जत्र्व् एकैकं तथा हनुः ॥
3.m: The pubic bone is one; in the back there are forty-five; / the neck has fifteen bones; the clavicles are one on each side, and likewise the jaw.

3.s:
tanmūle dve lalāṭākṣigaṇḍe nāsā ghanāsthikā /
pārśvakāḥ sthālakaiḥ sārdham arbudaiś ca dvisaptatiḥ //
3.d:
तन्मूले द्वे ललाटाक्षिगण्डे नासा घनास्थिका ।
पार्श्वकाः स्थालकैः सार्धम् अर्बुदैश् च द्विसप्ततिः ॥
3.m: At its base are two, two in the forehead, eyes, and temples; the nose is a solid bone; / the ribs together with their sockets and tubercles are seventy-two.

3.s:
dvau śaṅkhakau kapālāni catvāri śirasas tathā /
uraḥ saptadaśāsthīni puruṣasyāsthisaṃgrahaḥ //
3.d:
द्वौ शङ्खकौ कपालानि चत्वारि शिरसस् तथा ।
उरः सप्तदशास्थीनि पुरुषस्यास्थिसंग्रहः ॥
3.m: There are two temples, four cranial plates of the head, / and seventeen bones in the chest: this is the sum of a man's bones.

3.s:
gandharūparasasparśaśabdāś ca viṣayāḥ smṛtāḥ /
nāsikā locane jihvā tvak śrotraṃ ca indriyāṇi ca //
3.d:
गन्धरूपरसस्पर्शशब्दाश् च विषयाः स्मृताः ।
नासिका लोचने जिह्वा त्वक् श्रोत्रं च इन्द्रियाणि च ॥
3.m: Smell, form, taste, touch, and sound are taught as sense objects; / the nose, eyes, tongue, skin, and ear are the sense organs.

3.s:
hastau pāyur upasthaṃ ca jihvā pādau ca pañca vai /
karmendriyāṇi jānīyān manaś caivobhayātmakam //
3.d:
हस्तौ पायुर् उपस्थं च जिह्वा पादौ च पञ्च वै ।
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि जानीयान् मनश् चैवोभयात्मकम् ॥
3.m: The two hands, the anus, the genitals, the tongue, and the two feet— / one should know these as the five organs of action, and the mind shares the nature of both.

3.s:
nābhir ojo gudaṃ śukraṃ śoṇitaṃ śaṅkhakau tathā /
mūrdhāṃsakaṇṭhahṛdayaṃ prāṇasyāyatanāni tu //
3.d:
नाभिर् ओजो गुदं शुक्रं शोणितं शङ्खकौ तथा ।
मूर्धांसकण्ठहृदयं प्राणस्यायतनानि तु ॥
3.m: The navel, vitality, rectum, semen, blood, both temples, / the head, shoulders, throat, and heart are the seats of the vital breath.

3.s:
vapā vasāvahananaṃ nābhiḥ kloma yakṛt plihā /
kṣudrāntraṃ vṛkkakau bastiḥ purīṣādhānam eva ca //
3.d:
वपा वसावहननं नाभिः क्लोम यकृत् प्लिहा ।
क्षुद्रान्त्रं वृक्ककौ बस्तिः पुरीषाधानम् एव च ॥
3.m: The omentum, fat tissue, navel, trachea, liver, spleen, / small intestine, kidneys, bladder, and receptacle for faeces,

3.s:
āmāśayo 'tha hṛdayaṃ sthūlāntraṃ guda eva ca /
udaraṃ ca gudau koṣṭhyau vistāro 'yam udāhṛtaḥ //
3.d:
आमाशयो ऽथ हृदयं स्थूलान्त्रं गुद एव च ।
उदरं च गुदौ कोष्ठ्यौ विस्तारो ऽयम् उदाहृतः ॥
3.m: the stomach, heart, large intestine, anus, / abdomen, and both buttocks and pelvic organs: this is proclaimed as the full extent.

3.s:
kanīnike cākṣikūṭe śaṣkulī karṇapatrakau /
karṇau śaṅkhau bhruvau dantaveṣṭāv oṣṭhau kakundare //
3.d:
कनीनिके चाक्षिकूटे शष्कुली कर्णपत्रकौ ।
कर्णौ शङ्खौ भ्रुवौ दन्तवेष्टाव् ओष्ठौ ककुन्दरे ॥
3.m: The pupils, eye sockets, ear cavities, auricles, / ears, temples, eyebrows, gums, lips, buttocks,

3.s:
vaṅkṣaṇau vṛṣaṇau vṛkkau śleṣmasaṃghātajau stanau /
upajihvāsphijau bāhū jaṅghoruṣu ca piṇḍikā //
3.d:
वङ्क्षणौ वृषणौ वृक्कौ श्लेष्मसंघातजौ स्तनौ ।
उपजिह्वास्फिजौ बाहू जङ्घोरुषु च पिण्डिका ॥
3.m: groins, testicles, kidneys, breasts arising from accumulations of phlegm, / uvula, hips, arms, and the calf-muscles in the shanks and thighs,

3.s:
tālūdaraṃ bastiśīrṣaṃ cibuke galaśuṇḍike /
avaṭaś caivam etāni sthānāny atra śarīrake //
3.d:
तालूदरं बस्तिशीर्षं चिबुके गलशुण्डिके ।
अवटश् चैवम् एतानि स्थानान्य् अत्र शरीरके ॥
3.m: palate, belly, crown of the bladder, chin, tonsils, / and nape: these are the anatomical sites in this body.

3.s:
akṣikarṇacatuṣkaṃ ca paddhastahṛdayāni ca /
nava chidrāṇi tāny eva prāṇasyāyatanāni tu //
3.d:
अक्षिकर्णचतुष्कं च पद्धस्तहृदयानि च ।
नव छिद्राणि तान्य् एव प्राणस्यायतनानि तु ॥
3.m: The four pairs of eyes and ears, the feet, hands, and heart, / and the nine apertures are indeed the seats of the vital breath.

3.s:
śirāḥ śatāni saptaiva nava snāyuśatāni ca /
dhamanīnāṃ śate dve tu pañca peśīśatāni ca //
3.d:
शिराः शतानि सप्तैव नव स्नायुशतानि च ।
धमनीनां शते द्वे तु पञ्च पेशीशतानि च ॥
3.m: There are seven hundred veins, nine hundred ligaments, / two hundred arteries, and five hundred muscles.

3.s:
ekonatriṃśallakṣāṇi tathā nava śatāni ca /
ṣaṭpañcāśac ca jānīta śirā dhamanisaṃjñitāḥ //
3.d:
एकोनत्रिंशल्लक्षाणि तथा नव शतानि च ।
षट्पञ्चाशच् च जानीत शिरा धमनिसंज्ञिताः ॥
3.m: Know that there are twenty-nine hundred thousand, nine hundred, / and fifty-six vessels termed veins and arteries.

3.s:
trayo lakṣās tu vijñeyāḥ śmaśrukeśāḥ śarīriṇām /
saptottaraṃ marmaśataṃ dve ca saṃdhiśate tathā //
3.d:
त्रयो लक्षास् तु विज्ञेयाः श्मश्रुकेशाः शरीरिणाम् ।
सप्तोत्तरं मर्मशतं द्वे च संधिशते तथा ॥
3.m: Three hundred thousand hairs of the beard and head are known in embodied beings, / one hundred and seven vital points, and two hundred joints.

3.s:
romṇāṃ koṭyas tu pañcāśac catasraḥ koṭya eva ca /
saptaṣaṣṭis tathā lakṣāḥ sārdhāḥ svedāyanaiḥ saha //
3.d:
रोम्णां कोट्यस् तु पञ्चाशच् चतस्रः कोट्य एव च ।
सप्तषष्टिस् तथा लक्षाः सार्धाः स्वेदायनैः सह ॥
3.m: There are fifty-four crores, / and sixty-seven and a half lakhs of body hairs together with the sweat-ducts.

3.s:
vāyavīyair vigaṇyante vibhaktāḥ paramāṇavaḥ /
yady apy eko 'nuvetty eṣāṃ bhāvanāṃ caiva saṃsthitim //
3.d:
वायवीयैर् विगण्यन्ते विभक्ताः परमाणवः ।
यद्य् अप्य् एको ऽनुवेत्त्य् एषां भावनां चैव संस्थितिम् ॥
3.m: Even if divided, the ultimate atoms can be calculated by the wind-particles, / although someone alone perceives their development and persistence.

3.s:
rasasya nava vijñeyā jalasyāñjalayo daśa /
saptaiva tu purīṣasya raktasyāṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ //
3.d:
रसस्य नव विज्ञेया जलस्याञ्जलयो दश ।
सप्तैव तु पुरीषस्य रक्तस्याष्टौ प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
3.m: Nine handfuls should be known of chyle, ten of water, / seven of faeces, and eight of blood are proclaimed;

3.s:
ṣaṭ śleṣmā pañca pittaṃ tu catvāro mūtram eva ca /
vasā trayo dvau tu medo majjaikordhvam tu mastake //
3.d:
षट् श्लेष्मा पञ्च पित्तं तु चत्वारो मूत्रम् एव च ।
वसा त्रयो द्वौ तु मेदो मज्जैकोर्ध्वम् तु मस्तके ॥
3.m: six of phlegm, five of bile, four of urine, / three of muscle-fat, two of adipose tissue, one of marrow, and above in the head [one of brain-marrow];

3.s:
śleṣmaujasas tāvad eva retasas tāvad eva tu /
ity etad asthiraṃ varṣma yasya mokṣāya kṛty asau //
3.d:
श्लेष्मौजसस् तावद् एव रेतसस् तावद् एव तु ।
इत्य् एतद् अस्थिरं वर्ष्म यस्य मोक्षाय कृत्य् असौ ॥
3.m: the same amount of phlegm-vitality, and the same amount of semen. / Such is this unstable body, for the liberation of which he acts.

3.s:
dvāsaptatisahasrāṇi hṛdayād abhiniḥsṛtāḥ /
hitāhitā nāma nāḍyas tāsāṃ madhye śaśiprabham //
3.d:
द्वासप्ततिसहस्राणि हृदयाद् अभिनिःसृताः ।
हिताहिता नाम नाड्यस् तासां मध्ये शशिप्रभम् ॥
3.m: Seventy-two thousand channels called the wholesome and unwholesome / issue forth from the heart; in the midst of them is a moon-like radiant

3.s:
maṇḍalaṃ tasya madhyastha ātmā dīpa ivācalaḥ /
sa jñeyas taṃ viditveha punar ājāyate na tu //
3.d:
मण्डलं तस्य मध्यस्थ आत्मा दीप इवाचलः ।
स ज्ञेयस् तं विदित्वेह पुनर् आजायते न तु ॥
3.m: orb; dwelling in the middle of it is the Self, motionless like a lamp. / It is to be known; having known it here, one is not born again.

3.s:
jñeyaṃ cāraṇyakam ahaṃ yad ādityād avāptavān /
yogaśāstraṃ ca matproktaṃ jñeyaṃ yogam abhīpsatā //
3.d:
ज्ञेयं चारण्यकम् अहं यद् आदित्याद् अवाप्तवान् ।
योगशास्त्रं च मत्प्रोक्तं ज्ञेयं योगम् अभीप्सता ॥
3.m: One should know the Āraṇyaka which I obtained from the sun, / and the treatise on yoga spoken by me should be known by one seeking yoga.

3.s:
ananyaviṣayaṃ kṛtvā manobuddhismṛtīndriyam /
dhyeya ātmā sthito yo 'sau hṛdaye dīpavat prabhuḥ //
3.d:
अनन्यविषयं कृत्वा मनोबुद्धिस्मृतीन्द्रियम् ।
ध्येय आत्मा स्थितो यो ऽसौ हृदये दीपवत् प्रभुः ॥
3.m: Having made the mind, intellect, memory, and senses free from other objects, / the Self which resides in the heart like a lamp, the Lord, is to be meditated upon.

3.s:
yathāvidhānena paṭhan sāmagāyam avicyutam /
sāvadhānas tad abhyāsāt paraṃ brahmādhigacchati //
3.d:
यथाविधानेन पठन् सामगायम् अविच्युतम् ।
सावधानस् तद् अभ्यासात् परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति ॥
3.m: Reciting the chanting of the Sāman according to rule without mistake, / attentive, through that practice he attains the supreme Brahman.

3.s:
aparāntakam ullopyaṃ madrakaṃ prakarīṃ tathā /
auveṇakaṃ sarobindum uttaraṃ gītakāni ca //
3.d:
अपरान्तकम् उल्लोप्यं मद्रकं प्रकरीं तथा ।
औवेणकं सरोबिन्दुम् उत्तरं गीतकानि च ॥
3.m: The aparāntaka, the ullopya, the madraka, and the prakarī, / as well as the auveṇaka, the sarobindu, the uttara, and the songs,

3.s:
ṛggāthā pāṇikā dakṣavihitā brahmagītikā /
geyam etat tadabhyāsakaraṇān mokṣasaṃjñitam //
3.d:
ऋग्गाथा पाणिका दक्षविहिता ब्रह्मगीतिका ।
गेयम् एतत् तदभ्यासकरणान् मोक्षसंज्ञितम् ॥
3.m: the ṛc-hymn, the song-verse, the pāṇikā, and the brahmagītikā prescribed by Dakṣa— / by practicing the singing of these, known as [instruments of] liberation,

3.s:
vīṇāvādanatattvajñaḥ śrutijātiviśāradaḥ /
tālajñaś cāprayāsena mokṣamārgaṃ niyacchati //
3.d:
वीणावादनतत्त्वज्ञः श्रुतिजातिविशारदः ।
तालज्ञश् चाप्रयासेन मोक्षमार्गं नियच्छति ॥
3.m: one who knows the truth of lute-playing, is skilled in microtones and melodic types, / and knows rhythm, enters upon the path to liberation without effort.

3.s:
gītajño yadi yogena nāpnoti paramaṃ padam /
rudrasyānucaro bhūtvā tenaiva saha modate //
3.d:
गीतज्ञो यदि योगेन नाप्नोति परमं पदम् ।
रुद्रस्यानुचरो भूत्वा तेनैव सह मोदते ॥
3.m: If a knower of song does not attain the highest state through yoga, / he becomes an attendant of Rudra and rejoices with him.

3.s:
anādir ātmā kathitas tasyādis tu śarīrakam /
ātmanas tu jagat sarvaṃ jagataś cātmasaṃbhavaḥ //
3.d:
अनादिर् आत्मा कथितस् तस्यादिस् तु शरीरकम् ।
आत्मनस् तु जगत् सर्वं जगतश् चात्मसंभवः ॥
3.m: The self is taught to be beginningless, but its beginning is the physical body; / from the self arises the entire world, and the origin of the world is from the self.

3.s:
katham etad vimuhyāmaḥ sadevāsuramānavam /
jagadudbhūtam ātmā ca kathaṃ tasmin vadasva naḥ //
3.d:
कथम् एतद् विमुह्यामः सदेवासुरमानवम् ।
जगदुद्भूतम् आत्मा च कथं तस्मिन् वदस्व नः ॥
3.m: “How is this? We are bewildered. Tell us how the world, / with gods, asuras, and humans, arose, and how the self is within it.”

3.s:
mohajālam apāsyeha puruṣo dṛśyate hi yaḥ /
sahasrakarapannetraḥ sūryavarcāḥ sahasrakaḥ //
3.d:
मोहजालम् अपास्येह पुरुषो दृश्यते हि यः ।
सहस्रकरपन्नेत्रः सूर्यवर्चाः सहस्रकः ॥
3.m: When the snare of delusion is cast aside here, the Puruṣa is indeed perceived— / he who has a thousand hands, feet, and eyes, has the splendour of the sun, and is thousandfold.

3.s:
sa ātmā caiva yajñaś ca viśvarūpaḥ prajāpatiḥ /
virājaḥ so 'nnarūpeṇa yajñatvam upagacchati //
3.d:
स आत्मा चैव यज्ञश् च विश्वरूपः प्रजापतिः ।
विराजः सो ऽन्नरूपेण यज्ञत्वम् उपगच्छति ॥
3.m: He is the self, the sacrifice, the all-formed Prajāpati; / in the form of the food of Virāj, he attains the nature of the sacrifice.

3.s:
yo dravyadevatātyāgasaṃbhūto rasa uttamaḥ /
devān saṃtarpya sa raso yajamānaṃ phalena ca //
3.d:
यो द्रव्यदेवतात्यागसंभूतो रस उत्तमः ।
देवान् संतर्प्य स रसो यजमानं फलेन च ॥
3.m: The highest essence that arises from the renunciation of substance and deity, / that essence, having satisfied the gods and [endowed] the sacrificer with reward,

3.s:
saṃyojya vāyunā somaṃ nīyate raśmibhis tataḥ /
ṛgyajuḥ sāmavihitaṃ sauraṃ dhāmopanīyate //
3.d:
संयोज्य वायुना सोमं नीयते रश्मिभिस् ततः ।
ऋग्यजुः सामविहितं सौरं धामोपनीयते ॥
3.m: and united with wind and soma, is then drawn up by the rays; / ordained by the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas, it is brought to the solar realm.

3.s:
khamaṇḍalād asau sūryaḥ sṛjaty amṛtam uttamam /
yaj janma sarvabhūtānām aśanānaśanātmanām //
3.d:
खमण्डलाद् असौ सूर्यः सृजत्य् अमृतम् उत्तमम् ।
यज् जन्म सर्वभूतानाम् अशनानशनात्मनाम् ॥
3.m: From the circle of the sky, that sun creates the highest nectar, / which is the birth of all beings, both the eating and the non-eating.

3.s:
tasmād annāt punar yajñaḥ punar annaṃ punaḥ kratuḥ /
evam etad anādyantaṃ cakraṃ saṃparivartate //
3.d:
तस्माद् अन्नात् पुनर् यज्ञः पुनर् अन्नं पुनः क्रतुः ।
एवम् एतद् अनाद्यन्तं चक्रं संपरिवर्तते ॥
3.m: From that food [arises] sacrifice again, from sacrifice again food, and again sacrifice; / in this way this wheel without beginning or end revolves.

3.s:
anādir ātmā saṃbhūtir vidyate nāntarātmanaḥ /
samavāyī tu puruṣo mohecchādveṣakarmajaḥ //
3.d:
अनादिर् आत्मा संभूतिर् विद्यते नान्तरात्मनः ।
समवायी तु पुरुषो मोहेच्छाद्वेषकर्मजः ॥
3.m: The self is beginningless; there is no origin of the inner self; / but the composite individual soul is born of delusion, desire, hatred, and action.

3.s:
sahasrātmā mayā yo va ādideva udāhṛtaḥ /
mukhabāhūrupajjāḥ syus tasya varṇā yathākramam //
3.d:
सहस्रात्मा मया यो व आदिदेव उदाहृतः ।
मुखबाहूरुपज्जाः स्युस् तस्य वर्णा यथाक्रमम् ॥
3.m: From the mouth, arms, thighs, and feet of that thousand-formed primordial god / whom I have described to you, the social classes are born in order.

3.s:
pṛthivī pādatas tasya śiraso dyaur ajāyata /
nastaḥ prāṇā diśaḥ śrotrāt sparśād vāyur mukhāc chikhī //
3.d:
पृथिवी पादतस् तस्य शिरसो द्यौर् अजायत ।
नस्तः प्राणा दिशः श्रोत्रात् स्पर्शाद् वायुर् मुखाच् छिखी ॥
3.m: From his feet the earth was born, from his head heaven; / from his nostrils the vital breaths, from his ear the directions, from his skin wind, and from his mouth fire.

3.s:
manasaś candramā jātaś cakṣuṣaś ca divākaraḥ /
jaghanād antarikṣaṃ ca jagac ca sacarācaram //
3.d:
मनसश् चन्द्रमा जातश् चक्षुषश् च दिवाकरः ।
जघनाद् अन्तरिक्षं च जगच् च सचराचरम् ॥
3.m: From his mind the moon was born, and from his eye the sun; / from his loins the atmosphere, and the world with all that moves and is still.

3.s:
yady evaṃ sa kathaṃ brahman pāpayoniṣu jāyate /
īśvaraḥ sa kathaṃ bhāvair aniṣṭaiḥ saṃprayujyate //
3.d:
यद्य् एवं स कथं ब्रह्मन् पापयोनिषु जायते ।
ईश्वरः स कथं भावैर् अनिष्टैः संप्रयुज्यते ॥
3.m: “If it is so, O Brahmin, how is he born in sinful wombs? / How is that Lord conjoined with undesirable states of existence?

3.s:
karaṇair anvitasyāpi pūrvaṃ jñānaṃ kathaṃ ca na /
vetti sarvagatāṃ kasmāt sarvago 'pi na vedanām //
3.d:
करणैर् अन्वितस्यापि पूर्वं ज्ञानं कथं च न ।
वेत्ति सर्वगतां कस्मात् सर्वगो ऽपि न वेदनाम् ॥
3.m: Though endowed with organs, why has he no prior knowledge? / And being all-pervading, why does he not perceive all-pervading sensation?”

3.s:
antyapakṣisthāvaratāṃ manovākkāyakarmajaiḥ /
doṣaiḥ prayāti jīvo 'yaṃ bhavaṃ yoniśateṣu ca //
3.d:
अन्त्यपक्षिस्थावरतां मनोवाक्कायकर्मजैः ।
दोषैः प्रयाति जीवो ऽयं भवं योनिशतेषु च ॥
3.m: Through faults born of the actions of mind, speech, and body, / this individual soul goes to the state of an outcaste, a bird, or an immobile thing, and to existence in hundreds of wombs.

3.s:
anantāś ca yathā bhāvāḥ śarīreṣu śarīriṇām /
rūpāṇyapi tathaiveha sarvayoniṣu dehinām //
3.d:
अनन्ताश् च यथा भावाः शरीरेषु शरीरिणाम् ।
रूपाण्यपि तथैवेह सर्वयोनिषु देहिनाम् ॥
3.m: Just as there are endless states of being in the bodies of the embodied, / so too are there forms for embodied souls in all wombs in this world.

3.s:
vipākaḥ karmaṇāṃ pretya keṣāṃcid iha jāyate /
iha vāmutra vaikeṣāṃ bhāvas tatra prayojanam //
3.d:
विपाकः कर्मणां प्रेत्य केषांचिद् इह जायते ।
इह वामुत्र वैकेषां भावस् तत्र प्रयोजनम् ॥
3.m: The fruition of some actions occurs after death, of some here [in this life], / and of some either here or in the next world; mental disposition is the cause in that.

3.s:
paradravyāṇy abhidhyāyaṃs tathāniṣṭāni cintayan /
vitathābhiniveśī ca jāyate 'nyāsu yoniṣu //
3.d:
परद्रव्याण्य् अभिध्यायंस् तथानिष्टानि चिन्तयन् ।
वितथाभिनिवेशी च जायते ऽन्यासु योनिषु ॥
3.m: Coveting the property of others, dwelling on harmful thoughts, / and persisting in falsehood, one is born in lower wombs.

3.s:
puruṣo 'nṛtavādī ca piśunaḥ paruṣas tathā /
anibaddhapralāpī ca mṛgapakṣiṣu jāyate //
3.d:
पुरुषो ऽनृतवादी च पिशुनः परुषस् तथा ।
अनिबद्धप्रलापी च मृगपक्षिषु जायते ॥
3.m: A man who speaks untruth, is slanderous, harsh, / and given to incoherent babble, is born among beasts and birds.

3.s:
adattādānanirataḥ paradāropasevakaḥ /
hiṃsakaś cāvidhānena sthāvareṣv abhijāyate //
3.d:
अदत्तादाननिरतः परदारोपसेवकः ।
हिंसकश् चाविधानेन स्थावरेष्व् अभिजायते ॥
3.m: Devoted to taking what is not given, consorting with another's wife, / and injuring without scriptural sanction, one is born among immobile things.

3.s:
ātmajñaḥ śaucavān dāntas tapasvī vijitendriyaḥ /
dharmakṛd vedavidyāvit sāttviko devayonitām //
3.d:
आत्मज्ञः शौचवान् दान्तस् तपस्वी विजितेन्द्रियः ।
धर्मकृद् वेदविद्यावित् सात्त्विको देवयोनिताम् ॥
3.m: Knowing the self, pure, self-controlled, ascetic, having conquered the senses, / performing duty, and knowing the Vedic learning, a sāttvika person attains birth among the gods.

3.s:
asatkāryarato 'dhīra ārambhī viṣayī ca yaḥ /
sa rājaso manuṣyeṣu mṛto janmādhigacchati //
3.d:
असत्कार्यरतो ऽधीर आरम्भी विषयी च यः ।
स राजसो मनुष्येषु मृतो जन्माधिगच्छति ॥
3.m: Devoted to bad deeds, unsteady, undertaking bold enterprises, and sensual— / such a rājasa person, having died, attains birth among human beings.

3.s:
nidrāluḥ krūrakṛl lubdho nāstiko yācakas tathā /
pramādavān bhinnavṛtto bhavet tiryakṣu tāmasaḥ //
3.d:
निद्रालुः क्रूरकृल् लुब्धो नास्तिको याचकस् तथा ।
प्रमादवान् भिन्नवृत्तो भवेत् तिर्यक्षु तामसः ॥
3.m: Sleepy, cruel, greedy, atheistic, and a beggar, / negligent and of broken conduct—such a tāmasa person is born among animals.

3.s:
rajasā tamasā caivaṃ samāviṣṭo bhramann iha /
bhāvair aniṣṭaiḥ saṃyuktaḥ saṃsāraṃ pratipadyate //
3.d:
रजसा तमसा चैवं समाविष्टो भ्रमन्न् इह ।
भावैर् अनिष्टैः संयुक्तः संसारं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
3.m: Thus pervaded by rajas and tamas, wandering here, / joined with undesirable states, he enters the cycle of rebirth.

3.s:
malino hi yathā ādarśo rūpālokasya na kṣamaḥ /
tathāvipakvakaraṇa ātmajñānasya na kṣamaḥ //
3.d:
मलिनो हि यथा आदर्शो रूपालोकस्य न क्षमः ।
तथाविपक्वकरण आत्मज्ञानस्य न क्षमः ॥
3.m: For just as a tarnished mirror is not capable of reflecting an image, / so the [mind whose] faculties are unripened is not capable of knowledge of the self.

3.s:
kaṭver vārau yathāpakve madhuraḥ san raso 'pi na /
prāpyate hy ātmani tathā nāpakvakaraṇe jñatā //
3.d:
कट्वेर् वारौ यथापक्वे मधुरः सन् रसो ऽपि न ।
प्राप्यते ह्य् आत्मनि तथा नापक्वकरणे ज्ञता ॥
3.m: Just as sweet juice, though present, is not obtained / in an unripe bitter gourd, so consciousness is not found in the self when its faculties are unripened.

3.s:
sarvāśrayāṃ nije dehe dehī vindati vedanām /
yogī muktaś ca sarvāsāṃ yo na cāpnoti vedanām //
3.d:
सर्वाश्रयां निजे देहे देही विन्दति वेदनाम् ।
योगी मुक्तश् च सर्वासां यो न चाप्नोति वेदनाम् ॥
3.m: The embodied soul experiences sensation residing in its own body; / and a yogi is liberated who experiences no sensations of any kind.

3.s:
ākāśam ekaṃ hi yathā ghaṭādiṣu pṛthag bhavet /
tathātmā eko hy anekaś ca jalādhāreṣv ivāṃśumān //
3.d:
आकाशम् एकं हि यथा घटादिषु पृथग् भवेत् ।
तथात्मा एको ह्य् अनेकश् च जलाधारेष्व् इवांशुमान् ॥
3.m: For just as space, though one, becomes distinct in pots and other things, / so the self is one and many, like the sun in vessels of water.

3.s:
brahmakhānilatejāṃsi jalaṃ bhūś ceti dhātavaḥ /
ime lokā eṣa cātmā tasmāc ca sacarācaram //
3.d:
ब्रह्मखानिलतेजांसि जलं भूश् चेति धातवः ।
इमे लोका एष चात्मा तस्माच् च सचराचरम् ॥
3.m: Brahman, space, wind, fire, water, and earth are the primary elements; / these worlds and this self [arise from them], and from that [comes] all that moves and is still.

3.s:
mṛddaṇḍacakrasaṃyogāt kumbhakāro yathā ghaṭam /
karoti tṛṇamṛtkāṣṭhair gṛhaṃ vā gṛhakārakaḥ //
3.d:
मृद्दण्डचक्रसंयोगात् कुम्भकारो यथा घटम् ।
करोति तृणमृत्काष्ठैर् गृहं वा गृहकारकः ॥
3.m: Just as a potter makes a pot through the combination of clay, staff, and wheel, / or a builder makes a house with grass, earth, and wood,

3.s:
hemamātram upādāya rūpaṃ vā hemakārakaḥ /
nijalālāsamāyogāt kośaṃ vā kośakārakaḥ //
3.d:
हेममात्रम् उपादाय रूपं वा हेमकारकः ।
निजलालासमायोगात् कोशं वा कोशकारकः ॥
3.m: or a goldsmith makes a form using gold alone, / or a silkworm makes a cocoon through the union of its own saliva,

3.s:
kāraṇāny evam ādāya tāsu tāsv iha yoniṣu /
sṛjaty ātmānam ātmā ca saṃbhūya karaṇāni ca //
3.d:
कारणान्य् एवम् आदाय तासु तास्व् इह योनिषु ।
सृजत्य् आत्मानम् आत्मा च संभूय करणानि च ॥
3.m: so the self, taking up the causes and coming together with the organs / in various wombs in this world, creates itself.

3.s:
mahābhūtāni satyāni yathātmāpi tathaiva hi /
ko 'nyathaikena netreṇa dṛṣṭam anyena paśyati //
3.d:
महाभूतानि सत्यानि यथात्मापि तथैव हि ।
को ऽन्यथैकेन नेत्रेण दृष्टम् अन्येन पश्यति ॥
3.m: The great elements are real, and just so is the self; / for who otherwise sees with one eye what was seen with the other?

3.s:
vācaṃ vā ko vijānāti punaḥ saṃśrutya saṃśrutām /
atītārthasmṛtiḥ kasya ko vā svapnasya kārakaḥ //
3.d:
वाचं वा को विजानाति पुनः संश्रुत्य संश्रुताम् ।
अतीतार्थस्मृतिः कस्य को वा स्वप्नस्य कारकः ॥
3.m: Or who recognizes speech after hearing it repeatedly? / Who has memory of past things, or who is the maker of dreams?

3.s:
jātirūpavayovṛttavidyādibhir ahaṃkṛtaḥ /
śabdādiviṣayodyogaṃ karmaṇā manasā girā //
3.d:
जातिरूपवयोवृत्तविद्यादिभिर् अहंकृतः ।
शब्दादिविषयोद्योगं कर्मणा मनसा गिरा ॥
3.m: Filled with egoism on account of birth, appearance, age, conduct, and learning, / undertaking action toward objects such as sound through deeds, mind, and speech,

3.s:
sa saṃdigdhamatiḥ karmaphalam asti na veti vā /
viplutaḥ siddham ātmānam asiddho 'pi hi manyate //
3.d:
स संदिग्धमतिः कर्मफलम् अस्ति न वेति वा ।
विप्लुतः सिद्धम् आत्मानम् असिद्धो ऽपि हि मन्यते ॥
3.m: his mind doubting whether the fruit of action exists or not, / astray, though unaccomplished he considers himself accomplished.

3.s:
mama dārāḥ sutāmātyā aham eṣām iti sthitiḥ /
hitāhiteṣu bhāveṣu viparītamatiḥ sadā //
3.d:
मम दाराः सुतामात्या अहम् एषाम् इति स्थितिः ।
हिताहितेषु भावेषु विपरीतमतिः सदा ॥
3.m: Thinking ‘My wife, my sons, my ministers; I belong to them’—such is his condition; / he is always perverse in judgment concerning what is beneficial and harmful.

3.s:
jñeyajñe prakṛtau caiva vikāre cāviśeṣavān /
anāśakānalāghātajalaprapatanodyamī //
3.d:
ज्ञेयज्ञे प्रकृतौ चैव विकारे चाविशेषवान् ।
अनाशकानलाघातजलप्रपतनोद्यमी ॥
3.m: Making no distinction between the object of knowledge and the knower, or between primary nature and its modifications, / he is eager to end his life by starvation, fire, poison, or jumping into water.

3.s:
evaṃvṛtto 'vinītātmā vitathābhiniveśavān /
karmaṇā dveṣamohābhyām icchayā caiva badhyate //
3.d:
एवंवृत्तो ऽविनीतात्मा वितथाभिनिवेशवान् ।
कर्मणा द्वेषमोहाभ्याम् इच्छया चैव बध्यते ॥
3.m: Behaving thus, his soul undisciplined and committed to falsehood, / he is bound by action, by hatred and delusion, and by desire.

3.s:
ācāryopāsanaṃ vedaśāstrārtheṣu vivekitā /
tatkarmaṇām anuṣṭhānaṃ saṅgaḥ sadbhir giraḥ śubhāḥ //
3.d:
आचार्योपासनं वेदशास्त्रार्थेषु विवेकिता ।
तत्कर्मणाम् अनुष्ठानं सङ्गः सद्भिर् गिरः शुभाः ॥
3.m: Attendance upon the preceptor, discernment regarding the meaning of the Vedas and treatises, / performance of their rites, association with the virtuous, auspicious speech,

3.s:
stryālokālambhavigamaḥ sarvabhūtātmadarśanam /
tyāgaḥ parigrahāṇāṃ ca jīrṇakāṣāyadhāraṇam //
3.d:
स्त्र्यालोकालम्भविगमः सर्वभूतात्मदर्शनम् ।
त्यागः परिग्रहाणां च जीर्णकाषायधारणम् ॥
3.m: desisting from looking at or touching women, seeing oneself in all beings, / renunciation of possessions, wearing worn ochre robes,

3.s:
viṣayendriyasaṃrodhas tandrālasyavivarjanam /
śarīraparisaṃkhyānaṃ pravṛttiṣv aghadarśanam //
3.d:
विषयेन्द्रियसंरोधस् तन्द्रालस्यविवर्जनम् ।
शरीरपरिसंख्यानं प्रवृत्तिष्व् अघदर्शनम् ॥
3.m: restraint of the senses from sense-objects, avoidance of drowsiness and laziness, / critical reflection on the body, perceiving evil in active pursuits,

3.s:
nīrajastamasā sattvaśuddhir niḥspṛhatā śamaḥ /
etair upāyaiḥ saṃśuddhaḥ sattvayogy amṛtī bhavet //
3.d:
नीरजस्तमसा सत्त्वशुद्धिर् निःस्पृहता शमः ।
एतैर् उपायैः संशुद्धः सत्त्वयोग्य् अमृती भवेत् ॥
3.m: purification of sattva through the removal of rajas and tamas, freedom from craving, and tranquillity— / purified by these means, endowed with sattva, one becomes immortal.

3.s:
tattvasmṛter upasthānāt sattvayogāt parikṣayāt /
karmaṇāṃ saṃnikarṣāc ca satāṃ yogaḥ pravartate //
3.d:
तत्त्वस्मृतेर् उपस्थानात् सत्त्वयोगात् परिक्षयात् ।
कर्मणां संनिकर्षाच् च सतां योगः प्रवर्तते ॥
3.m: Through the presence of memory of the reality, through union with sattva, through the destruction / of actions, and through proximity to the virtuous, yoga proceeds.

3.s:
śarīrasaṃkṣaye yasya manaḥ sattvastham īśvaram /
aviplutamatiḥ samyak sa jātisaṃsmaratām iyāt //
3.d:
शरीरसंक्षये यस्य मनः सत्त्वस्थम् ईश्वरम् ।
अविप्लुतमतिः सम्यक् स जातिसंस्मरताम् इयात् ॥
3.m: At the dissolution of the body, he whose mind is fixed on purity [and] the Lord, / with an unwavering intellect, fully attains the recollection of his former births.

3.s:
yathā hi bharato varṇair varṇayaty ātmanas tanum /
nānārūpāṇi kurvāṇas tathātmā karmajās tanūḥ //
3.d:
यथा हि भरतो वर्णैर् वर्णयत्य् आत्मनस् तनुम् ।
नानारूपाणि कुर्वाणस् तथात्मा कर्मजास् तनूः ॥
3.m: For just as an actor colours his body with paints / creating various forms, so does the self [assume] bodies born of action.

3.s:
kālakarmātmabījānāṃ doṣair mātus tathaiva ca /
garbhasya vaikṛtaṃ dṛṣṭam aṅgahīnādi janmanaḥ //
3.d:
कालकर्मात्मबीजानां दोषैर् मातुस् तथैव च ।
गर्भस्य वैकृतं दृष्टम् अङ्गहीनादि जन्मनः ॥
3.m: Through defects of time, action, the self's seed, and likewise of the mother, / deformity of the embryo is observed, such as being born lacking limbs.

3.s:
ahaṃkāreṇa manasā gatyā karmaphalena ca /
śarīreṇa ca nātmāyaṃ muktapūrvaḥ kathaṃcana //
3.d:
अहंकारेण मनसा गत्या कर्मफलेन च ।
शरीरेण च नात्मायं मुक्तपूर्वः कथंचन ॥
3.m: Never before has this self been liberated from egoism, / mind, transmigration, the fruit of action, and the physical body.

3.s:
vartyādhārasnehayogād yathā dīpasya saṃsthitiḥ /
vikriyāpi ca dṛṣṭaivam akāle prāṇasaṃkṣayaḥ //
3.d:
वर्त्याधारस्नेहयोगाद् यथा दीपस्य संस्थितिः ।
विक्रियापि च दृष्टैवम् अकाले प्राणसंक्षयः ॥
3.m: Just as the persistence of a lamp depends on the combination of wick, base, and oil, / and its destruction is likewise observed, so occurs premature exhaustion of vital breath.

3.s:
anantā raśmayas tasya dīpavad yaḥ sthito hṛdi /
sitāsitāḥ karburūpāḥ kapilā nīlalohitāḥ //
3.d:
अनन्ता रश्मयस् तस्य दीपवद् यः स्थितो हृदि ।
सितासिताः कर्बुरूपाः कपिला नीललोहिताः ॥
3.m: Endless are the rays of him who dwells like a lamp in the heart: / white, black, variegated, tawny, dark blue, and red.

3.s:
ūrdhvam ekaḥ sthitas teṣāṃ yo bhittvā sūryamaṇḍalam /
brahmalokam atikramya tena yāti parāṃ gatim //
3.d:
ऊर्ध्वम् एकः स्थितस् तेषां यो भित्त्वा सूर्यमण्डलम् ।
ब्रह्मलोकम् अतिक्रम्य तेन याति परां गतिम् ॥
3.m: One of them extends upwards; piercing the orb of the sun / and passing beyond the realm of Brahmā, one attains through it the supreme goal.

3.s:
yad asyānyad raśmiśatam ūrdhvam eva vyavasthitam /
tena devaśarīrāṇi sadhāmāni prapadyate //
3.d:
यद् अस्यान्यद् रश्मिशतम् ऊर्ध्वम् एव व्यवस्थितम् ।
तेन देवशरीराणि सधामानि प्रपद्यते ॥
3.m: Through the hundred other rays of his that are also directed upwards, / one attains the bodies of gods along with their celestial abodes.

3.s:
ye 'nekarūpāś cādhastād raśmayo 'sya mṛduprabhāḥ /
iha karmopabhogāya taiḥ saṃsarati so 'vaśaḥ //
3.d:
ये ऽनेकरूपाश् चाधस्ताद् रश्मयो ऽस्य मृदुप्रभाः ।
इह कर्मोपभोगाय तैः संसरति सो ऽवशः ॥
3.m: Those multiform rays of his extending downwards, endowed with soft radiance— / by means of them, helpless, he transmigrates here to experience [the fruits of] action.

3.s:
vedaiḥ śāstraiḥ savijñānair janmanā maraṇena ca /
ārtyā gatyā tathāgatyā satyena hy anṛtena ca //
3.d:
वेदैः शास्त्रैः सविज्ञानैर् जन्मना मरणेन च ।
आर्त्या गत्या तथागत्या सत्येन ह्य् अनृतेन च ॥
3.m: Through the Vedas, the treatises along with higher knowledge, through birth and death, / through distress, departure, and return, through truth and falsehood,

3.s:
śreyasā sukhaduḥkhābhyāṃ karmabhiś ca śubhāśubhaiḥ /
nimittaśākunajñānagrahasaṃyogajaiḥ phalaiḥ //
3.d:
श्रेयसा सुखदुःखाभ्यां कर्मभिश् च शुभाशुभैः ।
निमित्तशाकुनज्ञानग्रहसंयोगजैः फलैः ॥
3.m: through the highest good, pleasure and pain, through good and evil deeds, / through the results born of the knowledge of omens, auguries, and planetary conjunctions,

3.s:
tārānakṣatrasaṃcārair jāgaraiḥ svapnajair api /
ākāśapavanajyotirjalabhūtimirais tathā //
3.d:
तारानक्षत्रसंचारैर् जागरैः स्वप्नजैर् अपि ।
आकाशपवनज्योतिर्जलभूतिमिरैस् तथा ॥
3.m: through the movements of stars and asterisms, waking states, and those born of dreams, / and likewise through space, wind, fire, water, and earth,

3.s:
manvantarair yugaprāptyā mantrauṣadhiphalair api /
vittātmānaṃ vedyamānaṃ kāraṇaṃ jagatas tathā //
3.d:
मन्वन्तरैर् युगप्राप्त्या मन्त्रौषधिफलैर् अपि ।
वित्तात्मानं वेद्यमानं कारणं जगतस् तथा ॥
3.m: through cosmic eras, the arrival of world-ages, and the fruits of mantras and medicinal herbs— / know the self as the object of knowledge and the cause of the universe.

3.s:
ahaṃkāraḥ smṛtir medhā dveṣo buddhiḥ sukhaṃ dhṛtiḥ /
indriyāntarasaṃcāra icchā dhāraṇajīvite //
3.d:
अहंकारः स्मृतिर् मेधा द्वेषो बुद्धिः सुखं धृतिः ।
इन्द्रियान्तरसंचार इच्छा धारणजीविते ॥
3.m: Egoism, memory, intellect, hatred, discernment, pleasure, resolve, / the movement between different sense organs, desire, bodily sustenance and life,

3.s:
svargaḥ svapnaś ca bhāvānāṃ preraṇaṃ manaso gatiḥ /
nimeṣaś cetanā yatna ādānaṃ pāñcabhautikam //
3.d:
स्वर्गः स्वप्नश् च भावानां प्रेरणं मनसो गतिः ।
निमेषश् चेतना यत्न आदानं पाञ्चभौतिकम् ॥
3.m: heaven, dream, the impulse of mental states, the movement of the mind, / blinking, consciousness, effort, and the acquisition of the five elements—

3.s:
yata etāni dṛśyante liṅgāni paramātmanaḥ /
tasmād asti paro dehād ātmā sarvaga īśvaraḥ //
3.d:
यत एतानि दृश्यन्ते लिङ्गानि परमात्मनः ।
तस्माद् अस्ति परो देहाद् आत्मा सर्वग ईश्वरः ॥
3.m: since these are observed as the marks of the Supreme Self, / therefore there is a self beyond the body, all-pervading and sovereign.

3.s:
buddhīndriyāṇi sārthāni manaḥ karmendriyāṇi ca /
ahaṃkāraś ca buddhiś ca pṛthivyādīni caiva hi //
3.d:
बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि सार्थानि मनः कर्मेन्द्रियाणि च ।
अहंकारश् च बुद्धिश् च पृथिव्यादीनि चैव हि ॥
3.m: The sense organs along with their objects, the mind, the organs of action, / egoism, intellect, and earth and the other [elements],

3.s:
avyaktam ātmā kṣetrajñaḥ kṣetrasyāsya nigadyate /
īśravaḥ sarvabhūtasthaḥ sann asan sad asac ca yaḥ //
3.d:
अव्यक्तम् आत्मा क्षेत्रज्ञः क्षेत्रस्यास्य निगद्यते ।
ईश्रवः सर्वभूतस्थः सन्न् असन् सद् असच् च यः ॥
3.m: the unmanifest, and the self are declared as the knower of the field of this field— / the Lord dwelling in all beings, who is existence, non-existence, and both existence and non-existence.

3.s:
buddher utpattir avyaktāt tato 'haṃkārasaṃbhavaḥ /
tanmātrādīny ahaṃkārād ekottaraguṇāni ca //
3.d:
बुद्धेर् उत्पत्तिर् अव्यक्तात् ततो ऽहंकारसंभवः ।
तन्मात्रादीन्य् अहंकाराद् एकोत्तरगुणानि च ॥
3.m: The arising of the intellect is from the unmanifest; from that arises egoism; / from egoism arise the subtle elements and the rest, having successively one additional quality.

3.s:
śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaś ca tadguṇāḥ /
yo yasmān niḥsṛtaś caiṣāṃ sa tasminn eva līyate //
3.d:
शब्दः स्पर्शश् च रूपं च रसो गन्धश् च तद्गुणाः ।
यो यस्मान् निःसृतश् चैषां स तस्मिन्न् एव लीयते ॥
3.m: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are their qualities; / whichever has emerged from whatever dissolves back into that very thing.

3.s:
yathātmānaṃ sṛjaty ātmā tathā vaḥ kathito mayā /
vipākāt triprakārāṇāṃ karmaṇām īśvaro 'pi san //
3.d:
यथात्मानं सृजत्य् आत्मा तथा वः कथितो मया ।
विपाकात् त्रिप्रकाराणां कर्मणाम् ईश्वरो ऽपि सन् ॥
3.m: Thus has it been declared to you by me how the self creates itself, / even though it is the Lord, through the ripening of the three kinds of action.

3.s:
sattvaṃ rajas tamaś caiva guṇās tasyaiva kīrtitāḥ /
rajastamobhyām āviṣṭaś cakravad bhrāmyate hy asau //
3.d:
सत्त्वं रजस् तमश् चैव गुणास् तस्यैव कीर्तिताः ।
रजस्तमोभ्याम् आविष्टश् चक्रवद् भ्राम्यते ह्य् असौ ॥
3.m: Purity, passion, and darkness are celebrated as its very qualities; / enveloped by passion and darkness, it is indeed whirled around like a wheel.

3.s:
anādir ādimāṃś caiva sa eva puruṣaḥ paraḥ /
liṅgendriyagrāhyarūpaḥ savikāra udāhṛtaḥ //
3.d:
अनादिर् आदिमांश् चैव स एव पुरुषः परः ।
लिङ्गेन्द्रियग्राह्यरूपः सविकार उदाहृतः ॥
3.m: Beginningless yet possessing a beginning, that very one is the supreme person; / having a form perceptible through bodily marks and senses, he is declared subject to modification.

3.s:
pitṛyāno 'javīthyāś ca yad agastyasya cāntaram /
tenāgnihotriṇo yānti svargakāmā divaṃ prati //
3.d:
पितृयानो ऽजवीथ्याश् च यद् अगस्त्यस्य चान्तरम् ।
तेनाग्निहोत्रिणो यान्ति स्वर्गकामा दिवं प्रति ॥
3.m: The space between the path of the ancestors, the Goat's Way, and Agastya— / along that path the performers of the Agnihotra, desiring heaven, proceed to the sky.

3.s:
ye ca dānaparāḥ samyag aṣṭābhiś ca guṇair yutāḥ /
te 'pi tenaiva mārgeṇa satyavrataparāyaṇāḥ //
3.d:
ये च दानपराः सम्यग् अष्टाभिश् च गुणैर् युताः ।
ते ऽपि तेनैव मार्गेण सत्यव्रतपरायणाः ॥
3.m: And those devoted to generosity, properly endowed with the eight virtues, / dedicated to the vow of truth, also go by that very path.

3.s:
tatrāṣṭāśītisāhasramunayo gṛhamedhinaḥ /
punarāvartino bījabhūtā dharmapravartakāḥ //
3.d:
तत्राष्टाशीतिसाहस्रमुनयो गृहमेधिनः ।
पुनरावर्तिनो बीजभूता धर्मप्रवर्तकाः ॥
3.m: There dwell eighty-eight thousand householder sages / who return again, serving as the seeds [of mankind] and promoters of duty.

3.s:
saptarṣināgavīthyantar devalokaṃ samāśritāḥ /
tāvanta eva munayaḥ sarvārambhavivarjitāḥ //
3.d:
सप्तर्षिनागवीथ्यन्तर् देवलोकं समाश्रिताः ।
तावन्त एव मुनयः सर्वारम्भविवर्जिताः ॥
3.m: Between the Seven Seers and the Serpent's Way, settled in the realm of the gods, / are just as many sages who have abandoned all worldly undertakings.

3.s:
tapasā brahmacaryeṇa saṅgatyāgena medhayā /
tatra gatvāvatiṣṭhante yāvad ābhūtasaṃplavam //
3.d:
तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण सङ्गत्यागेन मेधया ।
तत्र गत्वावतिष्ठन्ते यावद् आभूतसंप्लवम् ॥
3.m: Through austerity, celibate studenthood, abandonment of attachment, and wisdom, / having gone there, they remain until the dissolution of the elements.

3.s:
yato vedāḥ purāṇāni vidyopaniṣadas tathā /
ślokā sūtrāṇi bhāṣyāṇi yac ca kiṃcana vāṅmayam //
3.d:
यतो वेदाः पुराणानि विद्योपनिषदस् तथा ।
श्लोका सूत्राणि भाष्याणि यच् च किंचन वाङ्मयम् ॥
3.m: From whom [originate] the Vedas, the Purāṇas, the sciences and the Upaniṣads, / verses, aphorisms, commentaries, and whatever speech exists—

3.s:
vedānuvacanaṃ yajño brahmacaryaṃ tapo damaḥ /
śraddhopavāsaḥ svātantryam ātmano jñānahetavaḥ //
3.d:
वेदानुवचनं यज्ञो ब्रह्मचर्यं तपो दमः ।
श्रद्धोपवासः स्वातन्त्र्यम् आत्मनो ज्ञानहेतवः ॥
3.m: the recitation of the Veda, sacrifice, celibate studenthood, austerity, self-control, / faith, fasting, and mastery over oneself are the means of knowing the self.

3.s:
sa hy āśramair vijijñāsyaḥ samastair evam eva tu /
draṣṭavyas tv atha mantavyaḥ śrotavyaś ca dvijātibhiḥ //
3.d:
स ह्य् आश्रमैर् विजिज्ञास्यः समस्तैर् एवम् एव तु ।
द्रष्टव्यस् त्व् अथ मन्तव्यः श्रोतव्यश् च द्विजातिभिः ॥
3.m: He should indeed be sought after in this very manner by all the stages of life; / and he must be seen, contemplated, and heard of by the twice-born.

3.s:
ya enam evaṃ vindanti ya vāraṇyakam āśritāḥ /
upāsate dvijāḥ satyaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ //
3.d:
य एनम् एवं विन्दन्ति य वारण्यकम् आश्रिताः ।
उपासते द्विजाः सत्यं श्रद्धया परया युताः ॥
3.m: Those who know him thus, or those forest-dwelling twice-born / who worship the truth endowed with supreme faith—

3.s:
kramāt te saṃbhavanty arcir ahaḥ śuklaṃ tathottaram /
ayanaṃ devalokaṃ ca savitāraṃ savaidyutam //
3.d:
क्रमात् ते संभवन्त्य् अर्चिर् अहः शुक्लं तथोत्तरम् ।
अयनं देवलोकं च सवितारं सवैद्युतम् ॥
3.m: they successively attain the flame, the day, the bright fortnight, the northern / course [of the sun], the realm of the gods, the sun, and the realm of lightning.

3.s:
tatas tān puruṣo 'bhyetya mānaso brahmalaukikān /
karoti punarāvṛttis teṣām iha na vidyate //
3.d:
ततस् तान् पुरुषो ऽभ्येत्य मानसो ब्रह्मलौकिकान् ।
करोति पुनरावृत्तिस् तेषाम् इह न विद्यते ॥
3.m: Then a mind-born person, approaching them, leads them to the realm of Brahmā; / for them, there is no return to this world.

3.s:
yajñena tapasā dānair ye hi svargajito narāḥ /
dhūmaṃ niśāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣaṃ dakṣiṇāyanam eva ca //
3.d:
यज्ञेन तपसा दानैर् ये हि स्वर्गजितो नराः ।
धूमं निशां कृष्णपक्षं दक्षिणायनम् एव च ॥
3.m: Those men, however, who conquer heaven through sacrifice, austerity, and gifts, / successively attain the smoke, the night, the dark fortnight, the southern course [of the sun],

3.s:
pitṛlokaṃ candramasaṃ vāyuṃ vṛṣṭiṃ jalaṃ mahīm /
kramāt te saṃbhavantīha punar eva vrajanti ca //
3.d:
पितृलोकं चन्द्रमसं वायुं वृष्टिं जलं महीम् ।
क्रमात् ते संभवन्तीह पुनर् एव व्रजन्ति च ॥
3.m: the realm of the ancestors, the moon, wind, rain, water, and earth, / and they return again into this world.

3.s:
etad yo na vijānāti mārgadvitayam ātmavān /
dandaśūkaḥ pataṅgo vā bhavet kīṭo 'tha vā kṛmiḥ //
3.d:
एतद् यो न विजानाति मार्गद्वितयम् आत्मवान् ।
दन्दशूकः पतङ्गो वा भवेत् कीटो ऽथ वा कृमिः ॥
3.m: He who, having a self, does not understand this pair of paths / becomes a venomous serpent, a moth, an insect, or a worm.

3.s:
ūrusthottānacaraṇaḥ savye nyasyottaraṃ karam /
uttānaṃ kiṃcid unnāmya mukhaṃ viṣṭabhya corasā //
3.d:
ऊरुस्थोत्तानचरणः सव्ये न्यस्योत्तरं करम् ।
उत्तानं किंचिद् उन्नाम्य मुखं विष्टभ्य चोरसा ॥
3.m: With the upturned foot placed on the thigh, resting the upper hand on the left, / raising the upturned face slightly, and steadying the chin against the chest,

3.s:
nimīlitākṣaḥ sattvastho dantair dantān asaṃspṛśan /
tālusthācalajihvaś ca saṃvṛtāsyaḥ suniścalaḥ //
3.d:
निमीलिताक्षः सत्त्वस्थो दन्तैर् दन्तान् असंस्पृशन् ।
तालुस्थाचलजिह्वश् च संवृतास्यः सुनिश्चलः ॥
3.m: with closed eyes, established in purity, not letting the teeth touch the teeth, / keeping the motionless tongue against the palate, with mouth closed, perfectly still,

3.s:
saṃnirudhyendriyagrāmaṃ nātinīcocchritāsanaḥ /
dviguṇaṃ triguṇaṃ vāpi prāṇāyāmam upakramet //
3.d:
संनिरुध्येन्द्रियग्रामं नातिनीचोच्छ्रितासनः ।
द्विगुणं त्रिगुणं वापि प्राणायामम् उपक्रमेत् ॥
3.m: having restrained the collection of senses, seated on a seat neither too low nor too high, / he should undertake breath control doubled or tripled.

3.s:
tato dhyeyaḥ sthito yo 'sau hṛdaye dīpavat prabhuḥ /
dhārayet tatra cātmānaṃ dhāraṇāṃ dhārayan budhaḥ //
3.d:
ततो ध्येयः स्थितो यो ऽसौ हृदये दीपवत् प्रभुः ।
धारयेत् तत्र चात्मानं धारणां धारयन् बुधः ॥
3.m: Then the Lord, who dwells like a lamp in the heart, should be meditated upon; / and fixing the mind there, the wise man should practice concentration.

3.s:
antardhānaṃ smṛtiḥ kāntir dṛṣṭiḥ śrotrajñatā tathā /
nijaṃ śarīram utsṛjya parakāyapraveśanam //
3.d:
अन्तर्धानं स्मृतिः कान्तिर् दृष्टिः श्रोत्रज्ञता तथा ।
निजं शरीरम् उत्सृज्य परकायप्रवेशनम् ॥
3.m: Invisibility, memory, beauty, clairvoyance, clairaudience, / abandoning one's own body and entering another's body,

3.s:
arthānāṃ chandataḥ sṛṣṭir yogasiddher hi lakṣaṇam /
siddhe yoge tyajan deham amṛtatvāya kalpate //
3.d:
अर्थानां छन्दतः सृष्टिर् योगसिद्धेर् हि लक्षणम् ।
सिद्धे योगे त्यजन् देहम् अमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
3.m: and the creation of objects at will are indeed the marks of the perfection of yoga; / when yoga is perfected, one who casts off the body is fit for immortality.

3.s:
atha vāpy abhyasan vedaṃ nyastakarmā vane vasan /
ayācitāśī mitabhuk parāṃ siddhim avāpnuyāt //
3.d:
अथ वाप्य् अभ्यसन् वेदं न्यस्तकर्मा वने वसन् ।
अयाचिताशी मितभुक् परां सिद्धिम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
3.m: Or rather, practicing the Veda, having cast off rites, dwelling in the forest, / eating unbegged food, and eating in moderation, he may attain supreme perfection.

3.s:
nyāyāgatadhanas tattvajñānaniṣṭho 'tithipriyaḥ /
śrādhakṛt satyavādī ca gṛhastho 'pi hi mucyate //
3.d:
न्यायागतधनस् तत्त्वज्ञाननिष्ठो ऽतिथिप्रियः ।
श्राधकृत् सत्यवादी च गृहस्थो ऽपि हि मुच्यते ॥
3.m: One whose wealth is acquired righteously, devoted to knowledge of the truth, fond of guests, / performing ancestral rites, and speaking the truth—even a householder is liberated.

3.s:
mahāpātakajān ghorān narakān prāpya dāruṇān /
karmakṣayāt prajāyante mahāpātakinas tv iha //
3.d:
महापातकजान् घोरान् नरकान् प्राप्य दारुणान् ।
कर्मक्षयात् प्रजायन्ते महापातकिनस् त्व् इह ॥
3.m: Having reached the dreadful, severe hells born of mortal sins, / perpetrators of mortal sins are reborn here upon the exhaustion of their action.

3.s:
mṛgāśvasūkaroṣṭrāṇāṃ brahmahā yonim ṛcchati /
kharapulkasavenānāṃ surāpo nātra saṃśayaḥ //
3.d:
मृगाश्वसूकरोष्ट्राणां ब्रह्महा योनिम् ऋच्छति ।
खरपुल्कसवेनानां सुरापो नात्र संशयः ॥
3.m: The killer of a Brahmin enters the womb of a deer, horse, boar, or camel; / a drinker of liquor [enters the womb] of a donkey, a Pulkasa, or a Vena, without doubt.

3.s:
kṛmikīṭapataṅgatvaṃ svarṇahārī samāpnuyāt /
tṛṇagulmalatātvaṃ ca kramaśo gurutalpagaḥ //
3.d:
कृमिकीटपतङ्गत्वं स्वर्णहारी समाप्नुयात् ।
तृणगुल्मलतात्वं च क्रमशो गुरुतल्पगः ॥
3.m:
The stealer of gold attains the condition of a worm, an insect, or a moth,
and the violator of the guru's bed gradually attains the condition of grass, a bush, or a creeper.

3.s:
brahmahā kṣayarogī syāt surāpaḥ śyāvadantakaḥ /
hemahārī tu kunakhī duścarmā gurutalpagaḥ //
3.d:
ब्रह्महा क्षयरोगी स्यात् सुरापः श्यावदन्तकः ।
हेमहारी तु कुनखी दुश्चर्मा गुरुतल्पगः ॥
3.m:
The killer of a Brahmin becomes consumptive; the drinker of liquor, black-toothed;
the stealer of gold, foul-nailed; and the violator of the guru's bed, diseased in the skin.

3.s:
yo yena saṃvasaty eṣāṃ sa talliṅgo 'bhijāyate /
annahartāmayāvī syān mūko vāgapahārakaḥ //
3.d:
यो येन संवसत्य् एषां स तल्लिङ्गो ऽभिजायते ।
अन्नहर्तामयावी स्यान् मूको वागपहारकः ॥
3.m:
Whoever associates with any of these is born with that person's mark.
The stealer of food becomes sickly; the stealer of speech, mute.

3.s:
dhānyamiśro 'tiriktāñgaḥ piśunaḥ pūtināsikaḥ /
tailahṛt tailapāyī syāt pūtivaktras tu sūcakaḥ //
3.d:
धान्यमिश्रो ऽतिरिक्ताञ्गः पिशुनः पूतिनासिकः ।
तैलहृत् तैलपायी स्यात् पूतिवक्त्रस् तु सूचकः ॥
3.m:
The mixer of grains becomes possessed of a redundant limb; the slanderer, foul-nosed;
the stealer of oil becomes a cockroach; and the informer, foul-mouthed.

3.s:
parasya yoṣitaṃ hṛtvā brahmasvam apahṛtya ca /
araṇye nirjale deśe bhavati brahmarākṣasaḥ //
3.d:
परस्य योषितं हृत्वा ब्रह्मस्वम् अपहृत्य च ।
अरण्ये निर्जले देशे भवति ब्रह्मराक्षसः ॥
3.m:
Having seized another's wife, and having stolen a Brahmin's property,
one becomes a Brahmarākṣasa in a waterless wilderness.

3.s:
hīnajātau prajāyeta pararatnāpahārakaḥ /
patraśākaṃ śikhī hatvā gandhān chucchundarī śubhān //
3.d:
हीनजातौ प्रजायेत पररत्नापहारकः ।
पत्रशाकं शिखी हत्वा गन्धान् छुच्छुन्दरी शुभान् ॥
3.m:
The stealer of another's gems is born in a low caste;
having stolen leafy vegetables, a peacock; [having stolen] pleasant perfumes, a musk-rat.

3.s:
mūṣako dhānyahārī syād yānam uṣṭraḥ kapiḥ phalam /
jalaṃ plavaḥ payaḥ kāko gṛhakārī hy upaskaram //
3.d:
मूषको धान्यहारी स्याद् यानम् उष्ट्रः कपिः फलम् ।
जलं प्लवः पयः काको गृहकारी ह्य् उपस्करम् ॥
3.m:
A stealer of grain becomes a mouse; of a vehicle, a camel; [of] fruit, a monkey;
[of] water, a diving bird; [of] milk, a crow; and [of] household furnishings, a wasp.

3.s:
madhu daṃśaḥ palaṃ gṛdhro gāṃ godhāgniṃ bakas tathā /
śvitrī vastraṃ śvā rasaṃ tu cīrī lavaṇahārakaḥ //
3.d:
मधु दंशः पलं गृध्रो गां गोधाग्निं बकस् तथा ।
श्वित्री वस्त्रं श्वा रसं तु चीरी लवणहारकः ॥
3.m:
[A stealer of] honey becomes a gadfly; of meat, a vulture; of a cow, an iguana; and of fire, a heron;
[a stealer of] clothing becomes a leper; of flavored liquid, a dog; and the stealer of salt, a cricket.

3.s:
pradarśanārtham etat tu mayoktaṃ steyakarmaṇi /
dravyaprakārā hi yathā tathaiva prāṇijātayaḥ //
3.d:
प्रदर्शनार्थम् एतत् तु मयोक्तं स्तेयकर्मणि ।
द्रव्यप्रकारा हि यथा तथैव प्राणिजातयः ॥
3.m:
This has been stated by me only by way of illustration in the matter of theft;
for just as there are types of objects, so indeed are the species of living beings.

3.s:
yathākarma phalaṃ prāpya tiryaktvaṃ kālaparyayāt /
jāyante lakṣaṇabhraṣṭā daridrāḥ puruṣādhamāḥ //
3.d:
यथाकर्म फलं प्राप्य तिर्यक्त्वं कालपर्ययात् ।
जायन्ते लक्षणभ्रष्टा दरिद्राः पुरुषाधमाः ॥
3.m:
Having obtained the fruit according to their deeds in the animal state through the lapse of time,
the lowest of men are born destitute, devoid of auspicious bodily marks.

3.s:
tato niṣkalmaṣībhūtāḥ kule mahati bhoginaḥ /
jāyante vidyayopetā dhanadhānyasamanvitāḥ //
3.d:
ततो निष्कल्मषीभूताः कुले महति भोगिनः ।
जायन्ते विद्ययोपेता धनधान्यसमन्विताः ॥
3.m:
Then, having become free of taint, they are born into a great family as men of enjoyment,
endowed with learning, and provided with wealth and grain.

3.s:
vihitasyānanuṣṭhānān ninditasya ca sevanāt /
anigrahāc cendriyāṇāṃ naraḥ patanam ṛcchati //
3.d:
विहितस्याननुष्ठानान् निन्दितस्य च सेवनात् ।
अनिग्रहाच् चेन्द्रियाणां नरः पतनम् ऋच्छति ॥
3.m:
From not performing what is ordained, and from resorting to what is condemned,
and from the non-restraint of the senses, a man incurs a fall [into sin].

3.s:
tasmāt teneha kartavyaṃ prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye /
evam asyāntarātmā ca lokaś caiva prasīdati //
3.d:
तस्मात् तेनेह कर्तव्यं प्रायश्चित्तं विशुद्धये ।
एवम् अस्यान्तरात्मा च लोकश् चैव प्रसीदति ॥
3.m:
Therefore, penance must be performed here by him for purification;
thus both his inner self and the world are pleased.

3.s:
prāyaścittam akurvāṇāḥ pāpeṣu niratā narāḥ /
apaścāttāpinaḥ kaṣṭān narakān yānti dāruṇān //
3.d:
प्रायश्चित्तम् अकुर्वाणाः पापेषु निरता नराः ।
अपश्चात्तापिनः कष्टान् नरकान् यान्ति दारुणान् ॥
3.m:
Men who do not perform penance, who are devoted to sins,
and without remorse, go to painful, terrible hells:

3.s:
tāmisraṃ lohaśaṅkuṃ ca mahānirayaśālmalī /
rauravaṃ kuḍmalaṃ pūtimṛttikaṃ kālasūtrakam //
3.d:
तामिस्रं लोहशङ्कुं च महानिरयशाल्मली ।
रौरवं कुड्मलं पूतिमृत्तिकं कालसूत्रकम् ॥
3.m:
Tāmisra, Lohaśaṅku, Mahāniraya, Śālmalī,
Raurava, Kuḍmala, Pūtimṛttika, Kālasūtra,

3.s:
saṃghātaṃ lohitodaṃ ca saviṣaṃ saṃprapātanam /
mahānarakakākolaṃ saṃjīvanamahāpatham //
3.d:
संघातं लोहितोदं च सविषं संप्रपातनम् ।
महानरककाकोलं संजीवनमहापथम् ॥
3.m:
Saṃghāta, Lohitoda, Saviṣa, Saṃprapātana,
Mahānaraka, Kākola, Saṃjīvana, Mahāpatha,

3.s:
avīcim andhatāmisraṃ kumbhīpākaṃ tathaiva ca /
asipatravanaṃ caiva tāpanaṃ caikaviṃśakam //
3.d:
अवीचिम् अन्धतामिस्रं कुम्भीपाकं तथैव च ।
असिपत्रवनं चैव तापनं चैकविंशकम् ॥
3.m:
Avīci, Andhatāmisra, and likewise Kumbhīpāka,
Asipatravana, and Tāpana as the twenty-first.

3.s:
mahāpātakajair ghorair upapātakajais tathā /
anvitā yānty acaritaprāyaścittā narādhamāḥ //
3.d:
महापातकजैर् घोरैर् उपपातकजैस् तथा ।
अन्विता यान्त्य् अचरितप्रायश्चित्ता नराधमाः ॥
3.m:
Attended by terrible [sins] born of major sins, and likewise born of minor sins,
the lowest of men who have not performed penance go [to these hells].

3.s:
prāyaścittair apaity eno yad ajñānakṛtaṃ bhavet /
kāmato vyavahāryas tu vacanād iha jāyate //
3.d:
प्रायश्चित्तैर् अपैत्य् एनो यद् अज्ञानकृतं भवेत् ।
कामतो व्यवहार्यस् तु वचनाद् इह जायते ॥
3.m:
Guilt that was committed through ignorance departs through penances;
but [when done] intentionally, one becomes fit to associate with in this world only by scriptural declaration.

3.s:
brahmahā madyapaḥ stenas tathaiva gurutalpagaḥ /
ete mahāpātakino yaś ca taiḥ saha saṃvaset //
3.d:
ब्रह्महा मद्यपः स्तेनस् तथैव गुरुतल्पगः ।
एते महापातकिनो यश् च तैः सह संवसेत् ॥
3.m:
A killer of a Brahmin, a drinker of liquor, a thief, and likewise a violator of the guru's bed:
these are major sinners, as is whoever associates with them.

3.s:
gurūṇām adhyadhikṣepo vedanindā suhṛdvadhaḥ /
brahmahatyāsamaṃ jñeyam adhītasya ca nāśanam //
3.d:
गुरूणाम् अध्यधिक्षेपो वेदनिन्दा सुहृद्वधः ।
ब्रह्महत्यासमं ज्ञेयम् अधीतस्य च नाशनम् ॥
3.m:
Excessive reviling of gurus, censure of the Veda, slaying a friend,
and destruction of what has been studied are to be known as equal to slaying a Brahmin.

3.s:
niṣiddhabhakṣaṇaṃ jaihmyam utkarṣe ca vaco 'nṛtam /
rajasvalāmukhāsvādaḥ surāpānasamāni tu //
3.d:
